c-ien-phrb-pcore.notes: Confirms the 2024 split path-history-register result. The M2 P-core is identical.

c-ien-pcore-pht.text: Firestorm's longest-history pattern history table is four-way with a 10-bit index using PC bits 6 and 9 and a 16-bit tag
c-ien-pcore-pht.quote:
we can conclude that
the associativity of the PHT is four, and PC[6] and PC[9]
are involved in the index hash function ... On the P-cores
of M1, the PHT has a 10-bit index ... the PHT employs a 16-bit
tag.
c-ien-pcore-pht.notes: Firestorm; the PC input to the table is PC[18:2]. Confirms the 2024 Firestorm result. The M2 P-core is identical.

c-ien-counter-3bit.text: Every pattern history table entry uses a 3-bit saturating counter
c-ien-counter-3bit.quote:
we observe that PHT entries on
all tested cores contain a 3-bit saturating counter.
c-ien-counter-3bit.notes: Measured on all tested cores (M1 through M4, P and E), so it holds for Firestorm. Agrees with Tuby and Morrison.

c-ien-all-taken.text: On Firestorm every taken branch type updates the path history register, while not-taken conditional branches do not
c-ien-all-taken.quote:
Our results show that all types of taken branches are recorded
on M1-M3 processors and on the E-cores of the M4 processor.
c-ien-all-taken.notes: Tested direct and indirect jumps, taken and non-taken conditional branches, direct and indirect calls, and returns. Supports the shift-and-XOR update policy where not-taken conditional branches do not shift.

c-ien-ecore-phr-60.text: On the Icestorm core the path history register records 60 taken branches
c-ien-ecore-phr-60.quote:
After executing 100 branches (P-cores)
or 60 branches (E-cores), the PHR is set to the target value.
c-ien-ecore-phr-60.notes: Confirms Tuby and Morrison's Icestorm history length of 60. Table 2 lists the Icestorm PHRB at 16 and PC input PC[17:2].

c-ien-ecore-phrt-t48.text: On the Icestorm core the target-address path history register folds in nearly the whole target address, bits 48:2
c-ien-ecore-phrt-t48.quote:
On the E-cores, our measurements confirm that bits T[46:2] participate in the PHR
hash function ... it is reasonable to infer that T[48:2] is regarded as the footprint in the PHR update
function.
c-ien-ecore-phrt-t48.notes: T[46:2] confirmed directly, T[48:2] inferred from a kernel collision. Unlike Firestorm's T[31:2], the Icestorm core hashes almost the full target address, which defeats brute-force aliasing.

c-ien-ecore-pht.text: On the Icestorm core the longest-history pattern history table is four-way with a 9-bit index and a 16-bit tag
c-ien-ecore-pht.quote:
on the E-cores, the PHT has
a 9-bit index ... the PHT employs a 16-bit
tag.
c-ien-ecore-pht.notes: Four-way per Table 2. The P-core table has a 10-bit index, the E-core a 9-bit index.

c-ien-pht-shared-pcore.text: User-space out-of-place Spectre-PHT mistraining steers kernel branch prediction on Firestorm, so its pattern history table is shared between user and kernel
c-ien-pht-shared-pcore.quote:
out-of-place Spectre-PHT mistraining
succeeds on both the P-cores and the E-cores across all tested Apple
M1-M4 processors. This demonstrates that PHT entries trained in
user space can be used by kernel branches for branch prediction.
c-ien-pht-shared-pcore.notes: Confirms that Firestorm keeps no user or kernel isolation in the conditional predictor.

c-ien-pht-shared-ecore.text: User-space out-of-place Spectre-PHT mistraining also steers kernel branch prediction on Icestorm
c-ien-pht-shared-ecore.quote:
we successfully achieve
out-of-place Spectre attacks on the E-cores of the M1 as well as on
all core types across Apple M2-M4 processors.
c-ien-pht-shared-ecore.notes: Disagrees with Tuby and Morrison, who reported Icestorm user or kernel isolation and failed on the E-cores; iEnFlow attributes their failure to the Icestorm core hashing nearly the full target address.

c-ien-m4-pcore-nojumps.text: On the M4 performance core direct unconditional jumps are not recorded in the path history register
c-ien-m4-pcore-nojumps.quote: on the P-cores of the M4, direct jumps (i.e., the b instruction) are not captured.
c-ien-m4-pcore-nojumps.notes: A change from M1 through M3, where every taken branch type is recorded; the authors tie it to new M4 branch prediction mechanisms.

c-ilk-l1i-ways.text: Timing loops over chains of branches at congruent addresses find a 6-way L1I on the M1 P-cores
c-ilk-l1i-ways.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-l1i-ways.notes: M1 (P) row, Mac Mini; M1 Pro, M1 Max, A14 and M2 P-cores also show 6 ways. Disagrees with the 12 ways of c-mh-v8-l1i-12way; the registers read by PACMAN say 6 (c-pac-l1i-ways).

c-ilk-l1i-size.text: The M1 P-core L1I is 192 KiB in 512 sets, the size taken as the ways times the largest stride that avoids self-eviction
c-ilk-l1i-size.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-l1i-size.notes: M1 (P) row, Mac Mini; sets follow from size, line and ways.

c-ilk-l1i-line.text: The M1 P-core L1I line is 64 bytes
c-ilk-l1i-line.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-l1i-line.notes: M1 (P) row, Mac Mini. The line is the smallest offset that, applied to half of an over-full congruent set, brings a speedup.

c-ilk-l1d-ways.text: Timing loops over congruent addresses find an 8-way L1D on the M1 P-cores
c-ilk-l1d-ways.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-l1d-ways.notes: M1 (P) row, Mac Mini; M1 Pro, M1 Max, A14 and M2 P-cores also show 8 ways.

c-ilk-l1d-size.text: The M1 P-core L1D is 128 KiB in 256 sets
c-ilk-l1d-size.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-l1d-size.notes: M1 (P) row, Mac Mini; size is ways times the largest stride that avoids self-eviction.

c-ilk-l1d-line.text: The M1 P-core L1D line is 64 bytes
c-ilk-l1d-line.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.

c-ilk-l2-ways.text: A minimal eviction set for the M1 P-cluster L2 holds 12 lines, giving 12 ways and 8192 sets
c-ilk-l2-ways.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-l2-ways.notes: M1 (P) row, Mac Mini; M1 Pro and M1 Max give the same. Sets follow from the sysctl size and line. The eviction sets are found by group testing with a timer or the timerless gadget.

c-ilk-l2-size.text: The M1 P-cluster L2 is 12 MiB as reported by sysctl
c-ilk-l2-size.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-l2-size.notes: M1 (P) row, Mac Mini; the L2 size and line come from the macOS and iOS sysctl interface.

c-ilk-l2-line.text: The M1 P-cluster L2 line is 128 bytes as reported by sysctl, twice the 64 B L1 line
c-ilk-l2-line.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-l2-line.notes: M1 (P) row, Mac Mini. Every chip in the table shows 128 B L2 lines.

c-ilk-l2-phys-indexed.text: The L2 is physically indexed, so its sets cannot be found from virtual addresses and need eviction sets
c-ilk-l2-phys-indexed.quote: as the L2 cache is physically indexed and we therefore cannot retrieve
c-ilk-l2-phys-indexed.notes: Stated as background, without a test.

c-ilk-ice-l1i.text: The M1 E-core L1I is 128 KiB, 8 ways of 256 sets with 64 B lines
c-ilk-ice-l1i.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-ice-l1i.notes: M1 (E) row; agrees with the register read in c-pac-ice-l1i.

c-ilk-ice-l1d.text: The M1 E-core L1D is 64 KiB, 8 ways of 128 sets with 64 B lines
c-ilk-ice-l1d.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.

c-ilk-ice-l2.text: The M1 E-cluster L2 is 4 MiB, 16 ways of 2048 sets with 128 B lines
c-ilk-ice-l2.quote: Mac Mini (M1, 2020) (Macmini9,1) A2348 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-ice-l2.notes: M1 (E) row; size from sysctl, ways from eviction sets. The M1 Pro and M1 Max E-cluster rows give the same, marked unconfirmed.

c-ilk-a14-l2.text: The A14 P-cluster L2 is 8 MiB, 16 ways of 4096 sets with 128 B lines
c-ilk-a14-l2.quote: iPhone 12 (iPhone13,2) A2172 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-a14-l2.notes: A14 Bionic (P) row, iPhone 12; size from sysctl, ways from eviction sets. Its P-core L1I and L1D rows match the M1 P-core.

c-ilk-m2-l2.text: The M2 P-cluster L2 is 16 MiB, 16 ways of 8192 sets with 128 B lines
c-ilk-m2-l2.quote: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) (Mac14,2) A2681 ... Table 1: The cache organization of various Apple CPUs. W: Ways, S: Sets, CL: Cache Line size.
c-ilk-m2-l2.notes: M2 (P) row; size from sysctl, ways from eviction sets. Its P-core L1I and L1D rows match the M1 P-core.

c-ilk-a15-l2.text: The A15 P-cluster L2 is 12 MiB with 128 B lines, and most likely 12 ways of 8192 sets
c-ilk-a15-l2.quote: iPhone 13 mini (iPhone14,4) A2481 ... we could not confirm the results, but these are the most likely based on other Apple CPUs with similar cache organization
c-ilk-a15-l2.notes: A15 Bionic (P) row; the size is from sysctl, while the ways and sets are starred as unconfirmed guesses.

c-ilk-spec-mul-100.text: With a branch condition evicted from the caches, M-series P-cores execute about 100 dependent multiplies under speculation before a following probe load is no longer reached
c-ilk-spec-mul-100.quote: we see that Apple’s M series CPUs can execute about 100 mul instructions under speculation
c-ilk-spec-mul-100.notes: Stated for the M series as a whole (M1 and M2 alike); Figure 2 plots each chip with the condition evicted from L1 or from L2. 1000 trials per mul count, timed with the privileged cycle counter.

c-ilk-spec-300.text: Taking 3 cycles per multiply, the authors put the speculation window on recent Apple cores at up to about 300 cycles
c-ilk-spec-300.quote: modern Apple hardware has deep pipelines, with speculation windows running as long as 300 cycles
c-ilk-spec-300.notes: 100 multiplies (c-ilk-spec-mul-100) at Johnson's 3-cycle mul latency; the method section words the same product as about 300 instructions.

c-ilk-l2-inclusive.text: Traversing an L2 eviction set on one core evicts the victim's line from another core's L1, so the M1 P-cluster L2 is inclusive of the L1s
c-ilk-l2-inclusive.quote: Indeed, we find that the L2 cache of the Apple M1 is inclusive of the L1 caches.
c-ilk-l2-inclusive.notes: Cross-core test with a control set that leaves the victim alone. Disagrees with the non-inclusive, non-exclusive readings of c-mh-v3-l2-covering-tags-hint and c-mh-v3-dram-fill-l1-only.

c-ilk-l2-half-line.text: Touching only one 64 B half of each 128 B L2 line in the eviction set evicts the victim's L1 copy only now and then; touching both halves roughly triples the eviction rate
c-ilk-l2-half-line.quote: while accessing half of an L2 cache line occasionally results in evictions, accessing both halves approximately triples the success rate

c-ilk-l2-three-passes.text: One or two traversals of an L2 eviction set do not always evict the victim, while three always do
c-ilk-l2-three-passes.quote: accessing the eviction set more often results in higher eviction rates, with 3 access iterations guaranteeing eviction
c-ilk-l2-three-passes.notes: The set is shuffled before each traversal, and a spinlock hands control between attacker and victim threads.

c-ilk-timer-42ns.text: Unprivileged code on Apple systems gets only mach_absolute_time(), a 24 MHz (42 ns) timer
c-ilk-timer-42ns.quote: unprivileged code can only access the timer provided by mach_absolute_time(), which PACMAN reported to have a resolution of 24 MHz [64], or 42 ns

c-ilk-kperf-cycles.text: Privileged native code on macOS and iOS can read a cycle-accurate counter through the kperf API
c-ilk-kperf-cycles.quote: Both macOS and iOS allow privileged native code to read a cycle-accurate timer which is accessible via the kperf API

c-ilk-l1d-plru.text: Apple L1D caches use a pseudo-LRU replacement policy, which earlier work turned into a stable covert channel
c-ilk-l1d-plru.quote: abuses the pseudo least recently used (pLRU) eviction strategy of L1-D caches to construct a particularly stable covert channel on Intel and Apple CPUs
c-ilk-l1d-plru.notes: From Google's Leaky.page work; iLeakage's own M1 results rest on this channel.

c-ilk-no-meltdown.text: Unlike early Apple cores, recent ones show no sign of Meltdown-style reads across address spaces
c-ilk-no-meltdown.quote: While early versions of Apple hardware were susceptible to Meltdown [4], there is no indication of such vulnerabilities in newer Apple CPUs.

c-jia-fetch-page-split.text: Firestorm splits a fetch that crosses a page boundary into two cycles, so a loop placed across two pages pays one extra cycle per iteration
c-jia-fetch-page-split.quote: 把循环放在两个页的边界上，发现 Firestorm 微架构遇到跨页的取指时确实会拆成两个周期来进行
c-jia-fetch-page-split.notes: Chen notes that one-cycle cross-page fetch would need two iTLB lookups or paired page entries.

c-jia-fetch-16.text: With the loop's first instruction in the last 4 bytes of one page and the rest on the next, time per iteration rises by a cycle every 16 instructions, so Firestorm fetches 16 instructions per cycle
c-jia-fetch-16.quote: 可以看到每 16 条指令会多一个周期，因此 Firestorm 的前端取指宽度确实是 16 条指令
c-jia-fetch-16.notes: Agrees with c-mh-v4-fetch-16. The same loop kept within one page is limited by the back end instead.

c-jia-fetch-line.text: Sixteen instructions per cycle is one 64 B cache line, though the back end limits the observed rate to 8 per cycle
c-jia-fetch-line.quote: 虽然 Fetch 可以每周期 16 条指令，也就是一条 64B 的缓存行，由于后端的限制，只能观察到 8 的 IPC

c-jia-ice-fetch-8.text: The same cross-page test adds a cycle every 8 instructions on Icestorm, so Icestorm fetches 8 instructions per cycle
c-jia-ice-fetch-8.quote: 可以看到每 8 条指令会多一个周期，意味着 Icestorm 的前端取指宽度为 8 条指令

c-jia-sysctl-l1i.text: macOS reports a 192 KB L1I for the performance cores and 128 KB for the efficiency cores
c-jia-sysctl-l1i.quote: 通过 sysctl 可以看到，Firestorm 具有 192KB L1 ICache，Icestorm 具有 128KB L1 ICache ... hw.perflevel0.l1icachesize: 196608
c-jia-sysctl-l1i.notes: macOS sysctl values as read by Chen.

c-jia-guide-l1i-size.text: Apple's optimization guide gives every P-core from the A14 and M1 to the A18 and M4 a 192 KiB L1I
c-jia-guide-l1i-size.quote: 根据 Apple Silicon CPU Optimization Guide，从 M1 Family 到 M4 Family，A14 Bionic 到 A18 Family，P-Core 的 L1 ICache 的配置都是 192KiB

c-jia-guide-l1i-ways.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the P-core L1I as 6-way set associative
c-jia-guide-l1i-ways.quote: P-Core 的 L1 ICache 的配置都是 192KiB , 6-way, 64B lines
c-jia-guide-l1i-ways.notes: From Apple's optimization guide. Disagrees with l1i.assoc (12); agrees with c-ilk-l1i-ways and c-pac-l1i-ways.

c-jia-guide-l1i-line.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the P-core L1I 64 B lines
c-jia-guide-l1i-line.quote: P-Core 的 L1 ICache 的配置都是 192KiB , 6-way, 64B lines

c-jia-guide-ice-l1i.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the E-core L1I as 128 KiB with 64 B lines, 8-way on the M1 and A14 and 4-way from the M2 and A15 on
c-jia-guide-ice-l1i.quote: E-Core 的 L1 ICache 都是 128KiB , 64B lines，其中 M1 Family 和 A14 Bionic 是 8-way，其余处理器（M2 Family 和 A15 Bionic 开始）是 4-way

c-jia-l1i-192.text: A loop of NOPs ending in a branch runs at 8 instructions per cycle up to a 192 KB footprint and drops quickly to 2.22 beyond it, matching a 192 KB L1I
c-jia-l1i-192.quote: 可以看到 footprint 在 192 KB 之前时可以达到 8 IPC，之后则快速降到 2.22 IPC，这里的 192 KB 就对应了 Firestorm 的 L1 ICache 的容量

c-jia-ice-l1i-128.text: On Icestorm the same loop runs at 4 per cycle up to 128 KB and drops to 2.10 beyond, matching a 128 KB L1I
c-jia-ice-l1i-128.quote: 可以看到 footprint 在 128 KB 之前时可以达到 4 IPC，之后则快速降到 2.10 IPC，这里的 128 KB 就对应了 Icestorm 的 L1 ICache 的容量

c-jia-btb-1024.text: With an unconditional branch every 4 bytes, Firestorm takes one cycle per branch up to 1024 branches, then three cycles per branch up to 49152 branches
c-jia-btb-1024.quote: 可见在 1024 个分支之内可以达到 1 的 CPI，超过 1024 个分支，出现了 3 CPI 的平台，一直延续到 49152 个分支

c-jia-btb-l1i-plateau.text: The three-cycle plateau ends at 49152 branches, which is where 4-byte branches fill the 192 KB L1I, so branches missing the BTB still cost three cycles while their code stays in the L1I
c-jia-btb-l1i-plateau.quote: 第二个拐点 49152，对应的是指令 footprint 超出 L1 ICache 的情况：L1 ICache 是 192KB，按照每 4 字节一个 B 指令计算，最多可以存放 49152 条 B 指令
c-jia-btb-l1i-plateau.notes: Same tier as c-ox-btb-miss-bubble and c-mh-v4-btb-l0.

c-jia-btb-miss-late.text: Past the BTB's capacity the predictor no longer knows which instructions are branches, and a branch is found only after fetch or even decode, which costs the extra cycles
c-jia-btb-miss-late.quote: 超出 BTB 容量以后，分支预测时，无法从 BTB 中得到哪些指令是分支指令的信息，只能等到取指甚至译码后才能后知后觉地发现这是一条分支指令

c-jia-btb-8b.text: With a branch every 8 bytes the one-cycle limit falls to 512 branches and the three-cycle plateau ends at 24576, showing a set-associative BTB whose index loses sets when low PC bits are always zero
c-jia-btb-8b.quote: 可以看到 CPI=1 的拐点前移到 512 个分支，同时 CPI=3 的平台的拐点也前移到了 24576。拐点的前移，意味着 BTB 采用了组相连的结构

c-jia-btb-index.text: Spacing branches 2048 B or more apart leaves room for only two one-cycle branches, so the zero-bubble BTB has 512 sets of 2 ways indexed by PC bits 10:2
c-jia-btb-index.quote: 最终 CPI=1 的拐点定格在 2 条分支，此时分支的间距大于或等于 2048B ... 可以认为 Firestorm 的 BTB 是 512 Set 2 Way 的结构，Index 是 PC[10:2]

c-jia-btb-2way.text: The first-level BTB is 2-way set associative
c-jia-btb-2way.quote: 根据这个信息，可以认为 Firestorm 的 BTB 是 512 Set 2 Way 的结构
c-jia-btb-2way.notes: Against the direct-mapped guess of c-mh-v4-m1-nfp-dm.

c-jia-l1i-6way.text: Branches 32 KB or more apart allow only six on the three-cycle plateau, which Chen reads as a 192 KB L1I of 512 sets and 6 ways indexed by PC bits 14:6
c-jia-l1i-6way.quote: CPI=3 的拐点定格在 6 条分支，此时分支的间距大于或等于 32KB ... 同时也侧面佐证了 192KB L1 ICache 是 512 Set 6 Way，Index 是 PC[14:6]

c-jia-ice-btb-1024.text: On Icestorm with a branch every 4 bytes the cost steps from 1 to 3 at 1024 branches with no second step; at 8 bytes the steps fall at 512 and 16384, the L1I capacity
c-jia-ice-btb-1024.quote: 可以看到 1024 的拐点，1024 之前是 1 IPC，之后增加到 3 IPC。比较奇怪的是，没有看到第二个拐点 ... 第一个拐点前移到 512，第二个拐点出现在 16384
c-jia-ice-btb-1024.notes: The source writes IPC here for what the Firestorm runs call CPI.

c-jia-ice-btb-16b.text: With branches 16 bytes apart Icestorm's first step falls to 256, then a new two-cycle plateau lasts to 2048 and a third step comes at 8192, the L1I capacity
c-jia-ice-btb-16b.quote: 第一个拐点前移到 256，然后出现了一个 2 CPI 的新平台，2 CPI 的平台的拐点出现在 2048，第三个拐点出现在 8192，对应 L1 ICache 容量

c-jia-ice-btb-guess.text: Icestorm's irregular BTB results suggest either one BTB with a hashed index or two BTB levels organized to work over different ranges rather than simply in series
c-jia-ice-btb-guess.quote: 可能只有一级 BTB，但它的 Index 函数进行了一些 Hash 而非直接取 PC 某几位 ... 可能有两级 BTB，它们并非简单地级联，而是通过不同的组织方式，在不同的区间内发挥作用

c-jia-ice-iprefetch.text: Icestorm never exceeds three cycles per branch at 4-byte spacing, perhaps because the test is too small or because an instruction prefetcher brings code in once the footprint passes the 128 KB L1I
c-jia-ice-iprefetch.quote: 测试规模不够大，把分支数量继续增大，才能出现 CPI>3 的情况 ... 指令预取器在工作，当 footprint 大于 128KB L1 ICache 时，能提前把指令取进来

c-jia-guide-itlb.text: Apple's optimization guide gives every P-core from the A14 and M1 to the A18 and M4 a 192-entry L1 iTLB, 3 MiB of 16 KiB pages
c-jia-guide-itlb.quote: P-Core 的 L1 ITLB 配置都是一样的： 192 entries ，考虑到每个页是 16 KiB，对应 3 MiB 的内存
c-jia-guide-itlb.notes: From Apple's optimization guide. Disagrees with itlb.entries (128).

c-jia-itlb-192.text: With branches on separate pages, cost rises from 1 to 3 cycles from BTB conflict misses, then from 3 to 13 cycles at 192 pages, matching a 192-entry L1 iTLB
c-jia-itlb-192.quote: 从 1 Cycle 到 3 Cycle 的增加是由于 L1 BTB 的冲突缺失，之后在 192 个页时从 3 Cycle 快速增加到 13 Cycle，则对应了 192 项的 L1 ITLB 容量
c-jia-itlb-192.notes: Against the 128 entries PACMAN derives from 4 ways and 32 sets (c-pac-itlb-128).

c-jia-ice-itlb-128.text: Icestorm shows one step, from 1 to 8 cycles per branch at 128 pages, so its L1 iTLB holds 128 entries
c-jia-ice-itlb-128.quote: 只有一个拐点，在 128 个页时，性能从 1 Cycle 下降到 8 Cycle，意味着 L1 ITLB 容量是 128 项

c-jia-guide-uops.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the M1 P-core a maximum sustained rate of 8 uops per cycle and the E-core 4
c-jia-guide-uops.quote: M1 Family 的 Sustained uops Per Cycle 最大值，P-Core 是 8，E-Core 是 4

c-jia-guide-uops-m4.text: Apple's optimization guide raises the P-core's sustained uops per cycle to 9 on the M3 and 10 on the M4
c-jia-guide-uops-m4.quote: M3 Family 的 P-Core 提升到了 9，E-Core 和 M2 持平；M4 Family 的 P-Core 进一步提升到了 10

c-jia-decode-8.text: Firestorm reaches at most 8 instructions per cycle, so decode is at least 8 wide; a wider decoder is not ruled out
c-jia-decode-8.quote: Firestorm 最大观察到 8 IPC，Icestorm 最大观察到 4 IPC，那么 Decode 宽度也至少是这么多，暂时也不能排除有更大的 Decode 宽度

c-jia-ice-decode-4.text: Icestorm reaches at most 4 instructions per cycle, so its decode is at least 4 wide
c-jia-ice-decode-4.quote: Icestorm 最大观察到 4 IPC，那么 Decode 宽度也至少是这么多

c-jia-ras-50.text: Average time per call jumps once the call chain is 50 deep, so Firestorm's return stack holds 50 entries
c-jia-ras-50.quote: 可以看到调用链深度为 50 时性能突然变差，因此 Firestorm 的 Return Stack 深度为 50

c-jia-ice-ras-32.text: On Icestorm the time per call jumps at a call depth of 32, so its return stack holds 32 entries
c-jia-ice-ras-32.quote: 可以看到调用链深度为 32 时性能突然变差，因此 Icestorm 的 Return Stack 深度为 32

c-jia-ice-phr.text: Icestorm keeps a 60-bit target path history and a 16-bit branch-address path history, both updated on taken branches by shifting one bit and XORing in target bits 47:2 and branch bits 5:2
c-jia-ice-phr.quote: 使用 60 位的 Path History Register for Target(PHRT) 以及 16 位的 Path History Register for Branch(PHRB)，每次执行 taken branch 时更新 ... PHRTnew = (PHRTold << 1) xor T[47:2]
c-jia-ice-phr.notes: Same method as Chen's Firestorm paper. c-ien-ecore-phrt-t48 gives target bits 48:2.

c-jia-int-spec-362.text: The integer register probe steps at 362 instructions; this counts registers free for speculation, and the register file also holds the architectural registers, at least 32
c-jia-int-spec-362.quote: 32b/64b int：测试 speculative 32/64 位整数寄存器的数量，拐点在 362 ... 注意这里测试的都是能够用于预测执行的寄存器数量，实际的物理寄存器堆还需要保存架构寄存器

c-jia-fp-spec-382.text: The FP register probe with 32-bit FP results steps at 382, the FP registers free for speculation
c-jia-fp-spec-382.quote: 32b fp：测试 speculative 32 位浮点寄存器的数量，拐点在 382

c-jia-flags-spec-123.text: The NZCV flags probe steps at 123, the flags registers free for speculation
c-jia-flags-spec-123.quote: flags：测试 speculative NZCV 寄存器的数量，拐点在 123

c-jia-ice-prf.text: On Icestorm the speculative register probes step at 77 integer, 74 FP and 38 flags registers
c-jia-ice-prf.quote: 32b/64b int：测试 speculative 32/64 位整数寄存器的数量，拐点在 77 ... 32b fp：测试 speculative 32 位浮点寄存器的数量，拐点在 74 ... 拐点在 38

c-jia-sysctl-l1d.text: macOS reports a 128 KB L1D for the performance cores and 64 KB for the efficiency cores
c-jia-sysctl-l1d.quote: Firestorm 具有 128KB L1 DCache，Icestorm 具有 64KB L1 DCache ... hw.perflevel0.l1dcachesize: 131072
c-jia-sysctl-l1d.notes: macOS sysctl values as read by Chen.

c-jia-guide-l1d.text: Apple's optimization guide gives every P-core from the A14 and M1 to the A18 and M4 a 128 KiB, 8-way L1D with 64 B lines
c-jia-guide-l1d.quote: P-Core 的 L1 DCache 都是 128KiB, 8-way, 64B lines 的配置
c-jia-guide-l1d.notes: From Apple's optimization guide. The E-core L1D is given as 64 KiB, 8-way, 64 B lines.

c-jia-l1d-128.text: A pointer chase shows a clear step at a 128 KB footprint, the L1D capacity
c-jia-l1d-128.quote: 可以看到 128KB 出现了明显的拐点，对应的就是 128KB 的 L1 DCache 容量

c-jia-l1d-lat-3.text: A pointer chase within the L1D takes 3 cycles per load
c-jia-l1d-lat-3.quote: 可以看到 128KB 出现了明显的拐点，对应的就是 128KB 的 L1 DCache 容量，和官方信息一致。L1 DCache 范围内延迟是 3 cycle

c-jia-past-l1d-16.text: Just past the L1D the pointer chase rises to 16 cycles per load
c-jia-past-l1d-16.quote: L1 DCache 范围内延迟是 3 cycle，之后提升到 16 cycle
c-jia-past-l1d-16.notes: The source does not name the level; l2.latency holds 17.

c-jia-ice-l1d.text: On Icestorm the pointer chase steps at 64 KB, the L1D capacity, with 3 cycles per load inside it and 14 beyond
c-jia-ice-l1d.quote: 可以看到 64KB 出现了明显的拐点，对应的就是 64KB 的 L1 DCache 容量，和官方信息一致。L1 DCache 范围内延迟是 3 cycle，之后提升到 14 cycle

c-jia-guide-dtlb.text: From Apple's optimization guide, the M1 P-core L1 dTLB holds 160 entries and the E-core 128
c-jia-guide-dtlb.quote: 因此，M1 的 P-Core L1 DTLB 容量是 160，E-Core L1 DTLB 容量是 128

c-jia-guide-a14-dtlb.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the A14, A15 and M2 P-cores a 256-entry L1 dTLB, against 160 on the M1
c-jia-guide-a14-dtlb.quote: 除了 M2 Family、A14 Bionic 和 A15 Bionic 的 L1 DTLB 是 256 entries 以外，其余的 M1 Family、M3 Family 到 M4 Family，A16 Bionic 到 A18 Family 的 L1 DTLB 都是 160 entries
c-jia-guide-a14-dtlb.notes: From Apple's optimization guide. Matches the 256 of c-at-l1-tlb.

c-jia-dtlb-160.text: A pointer chase with one pointer per page slows from 160 pages and settles at 9 cycles per load by 250 pages, so the L1 dTLB holds 160 entries; the 9 cycles include an L2 TLB hit
c-jia-dtlb-160.quote: 从 160 个页开始性能下降，到 250 个页时性能稳定在 9 CPI，认为 Firestorm 的 L1 DTLB 有 160 项

c-jia-dtlb-5way.text: Spreading pointers 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 pages apart moves the step to 80, 40, 20, 10 and 5 pages, and 64 pages apart stays at 5, so the L1 dTLB is 5-way with 32 sets indexed by VA bits 18:14
c-jia-dtlb-5way.quote: 每 32 个页一个指针，拐点变成 5；每 64 个页一个指针，拐点依然是 5。说明 Firestorm 的 L1 DTLB 是 5 路组相连，32 个 Set，Index 是 VA[18:14]
c-jia-dtlb-5way.value: 5-way set associative, indexed by VA bits 14-18

c-jia-ice-dtlb.text: Icestorm's L1 dTLB holds 128 entries, 4-way with 32 sets indexed by VA bits 18:14; past it loads settle at 10 cycles
c-jia-ice-dtlb.quote: 从 128 个页开始性能下降，到 160 个页时性能稳定在 10 CPI，认为 Icestorm 的 L1 DTLB 有 128 项 ... 说明 Icestorm 的 L1 DTLB 是 4 路组相连，32 个 Set，Index 是 VA[18:14]

c-jia-ldst-mix.text: Per cycle Firestorm completes 3 loads with 1 store, 2 loads with 2 stores, 1 load with 2 stores, or 2 stores (128-bit accesses)
c-jia-ldst-mix.quote: 实测 Firestorm 每个周期可以完成 ... 3x 128b Load + 1x 128b Store ... 2x 128b Load + 2x 128b Store ... 1x 128b Load + 2x 128b Store

c-jia-stores-2.text: At most 3 loads or 2 stores execute per cycle
c-jia-stores-2.quote: 访存方面，每周期最多 3 Load 或者 2 Store

c-jia-load-bw-48.text: Widening each access from 128 to 256 bits halves the instruction rate and leaves bandwidth unchanged, so peak read bandwidth is 48 B per cycle
c-jia-load-bw-48.quote: 如果把每条指令的访存位宽从 128b 改成 256b，读写带宽不变，指令吞吐减半。也就是说最大的读带宽是 48B/cyc

c-jia-store-bw-32.text: Peak write bandwidth is 32 B per cycle, and peak read and peak write cannot be reached together
c-jia-store-bw-32.quote: 最大的写带宽是 32B/cyc，二者不能同时达到

c-jia-ice-ldst.text: Per cycle Icestorm completes 2 loads, 1 load with 1 store, or 1 store, for at most 32 B per cycle read and 16 B per cycle written
c-jia-ice-ldst.quote: 实测 Icestorm 每个周期可以完成 ... 也就是说最大的读带宽是 32B/cyc，最大的写带宽是 16B/cyc

c-jia-mdp-70.text: Repeating a store and a load to one address, the address-dependent pattern slows past 70 loads, while the data-dependent pattern has no clear threshold but starts a small rise at 84
c-jia-mdp-70.quote: 数据依赖没有明显的阈值，但从 84 开始出现了一个小的增长，且斜率不为零；地址依赖的阈值是 70
c-jia-mdp-70.notes: Handley reads a similar knee as a predictor of about 74 entries (c-mh-v1-lsdp-74-chained).

c-jia-ice-mdp-13.text: On Icestorm both the data-dependent and the address-dependent patterns slow past 13 loads
c-jia-ice-mdp-13.quote: 数据依赖和地址依赖的阈值都是 13

c-jia-stlf-overlap.text: Every overlapping store and load of 8 to 64 bits forwards whatever the offset, even when the load or store crosses a 64 B line, at the cost of one more cycle
c-jia-stlf-overlap.quote: 所有 Store 和 Load Overlap 的情况，无论地址偏移，都能成功转发。甚至在 Load 或 Store 跨越 64B 缓存行边界时，也可以成功转发，代价是多一个周期

c-jia-stlf-multi.text: A load that needs data from two, four or eight stores forwards at any offset unless the data crosses a line, taking 1 to 4 cycles more than forwarding from one store
c-jia-stlf-multi.quote: 一个 Load 需要转发两个、四个甚至八个 Store 的数据时，如果数据跨越缓存行，则不能转发，但其他情况下，无论地址偏移，都可以转发，只是比从单个 Store 转发需要多耗费 1-4 个周期

c-jia-stlf-latency.text: A successful forward takes 7.5 cycles, and a failed forward across a line takes 28 cycles or more
c-jia-stlf-latency.quote: 成功转发时 7.5 cycle，跨缓存行且转发失败时 28+ cycle
c-jia-stlf-latency.notes: Latency per forwarded store and load in his test; c-mh-v1-store-load-pair-6 gives 6.

c-jia-ice-stlf.text: On Icestorm any overlap between a load and earlier stores costs 10 cycles, however many stores overlap and whether or not a line is crossed
c-jia-ice-stlf.quote: 在 Icestorm 上，如果 Load 和 Store 访问范围出现重叠，则需要 10 Cycle，无论是和几个 Store 重叠，也无论是否跨缓存行

c-jia-guide-ptr-chase.text: Apple's optimization guide describes fast pointer chasing with 3-cycle latency when a load's base register is the previous load's destination
c-jia-guide-ptr-chase.quote: Apple 实现了 fast pointer chasing with a 3-cycle latency，要求后一个 load 的 base register 和前一个 load 的 destination register 相同

c-jia-ptr-chase-3.text: A load feeding the next load's base runs at 3 cycles with no offset, an immediate offset, a register offset, or from the first register of an LDP; an access crossing an 8 B boundary takes 4
c-jia-ptr-chase-3.quote: 实测 Firestorm 的 Load to use latency 针对 pointer chasing 场景做了优化，在下列的场景下可以达到 3 cycle ... ldp x0, x1, [x0] ：load pair 的第一个目的寄存器转发到基地址，无偏移 如果访存跨越了 8B 边界，则退化到 4 cycle

c-jia-load-use-4.text: Load-to-use latency is 4 cycles when the result feeds an ALU, the index register of the next load, or when it is the second register of an LDP feeding the next base
c-jia-load-use-4.quote: 在下列场景下 Load to use latency 则是 4 cycle ... load 的目的寄存器作为 alu 的源寄存器 ... ldp x1, x0, [x0] ：load pair 的第二个目的寄存器转发到基地址，无偏移

c-jia-ice-ptr-chase.text: Icestorm has the same 3-cycle pointer-chase cases and 4-cycle cases as Firestorm; crossing an 8, 16 or 32 B boundary still takes 3 cycles and crossing a 64 B boundary takes 7
c-jia-ice-ptr-chase.quote: 实测 Icestorm 的 Load to use latency 针对 pointer chasing 场景做了优化 ... 如果访存跨越了 8B/16B/32B 边界，依然是 3 cycle；跨越了 64B 边界则退化到 7 cycle

c-jia-utag.text: AMD's utag test shows the same effects on the M1, read as a virtual-address utag way predictor whose 8-bit tag XOR-folds VA bits 47:14, identical on Firestorm and Icestorm
c-jia-utag.quote: 猜想它也用了类似的基于虚拟地址的 UTag/Way Predictor 方案，并测出来它的 UTag 也有 8 bit，Firestorm 和 Icestorm 都是相同的 ... 一共有 8 bit，由 VA[47:14] 折叠而来
c-jia-utag.notes: The eight folds run from VA bits 14, 22, 30, 38 and 46 to VA bits 21, 29, 37 and 45.

c-jia-guide-int-units.text: Apple's optimization guide lists six integer units for the M1 P-core: ALU/f with BRc/i, ALU/f with BRc, ALU/f, ALU with MUL, MAC and MISC, ALU with MUL and DIV, and ALU
c-jia-guide-int-units.quote: M1 Family 的 P-Core 包括如下计算单元 ... ALU/f, BRc/i ... ALU/f, BRc ... ALU, MUL, MAC, MISC ... ALU, MUL, DIV

c-jia-guide-fp-units.text: Apple's optimization guide lists four FP/SIMD units for the M1 P-core; one adds FDIV, FCMP and SHA, two add moves to GPRs and FCSEL, and all four multiply
c-jia-guide-fp-units.quote: GENERAL, MOVE2GPR, FCMPf, FCSELf, FDIV, MUL, SHA ... GENERAL, MOVE2GPR, FCSELf, MUL ... GENERAL, MUL

c-jia-guide-lsu.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the P-core a burst of 3 load uops, 2 store-address uops and 2 store-data uops per cycle, and a sustained 4 uops of which 2 write the cache
c-jia-guide-lsu.quote: Burst: 3 load uops, 2 store uops (address part), and 2 store uops (data part) ... Sustained: 4 uops, 2 write into the cache
c-jia-guide-lsu.notes: From Apple's optimization guide. Chen's own tests did not separate the store address and data parts.

c-jia-addi-6.text: ADD with an immediate runs at 6 per cycle, so six ALUs; ADD, UBFM and SBFM sometimes measure 4.6 to 4.7 and sometimes 6, which Chen suspects is a low-power mode
c-jia-addi-6.quote: 从 addi 的指令来看，有 6 个 ALU，能够执行基本的整数指令（add/ubfm/sbfm 的吞吐有时候测出来 4.6-4.7，有时候测出来 6，怀疑是进入了什么低功耗模式）
c-jia-addi-6.notes: The register_security_tag mechanism describes a similar slowdown to about 4-wide.

c-jia-int-roles.text: Mixed-throughput tests give the six integer units as two with ALU, CSEL, branch and MRS NZCV, one with ALU, CSEL and FP-to-integer moves, one with ALU and those moves, one with ALU, MUL, MADD and CRC, and one with ALU and MUL
c-jia-int-roles.quote: 小结：Firestorm 的执行单元如下 ... alu + csel + branch + mrs nzcv ... alu + csel + fmov f2i ... alu + fmov f2i ... alu + mul + madd + crc ... alu + mul
c-jia-int-roles.value: 2x alu+csel+branch+mrs nzcv; alu+csel+fmov f2i; alu+fmov f2i; alu+mul+madd+crc; alu+mul
c-jia-int-roles.notes: Matches Johnson's unit roles (c-dj-int-roles) for the instructions tested.

c-jia-fp-roles.text: All four FP/SIMD units run basic FP/SIMD and AES; one also runs FDIV, FRECPE, FRECPX, FRSQRTE and FSQRT, and two run FP-to-integer moves and conversions
c-jia-fp-roles.quote: basic fp/asimd ops + aes + fdiv + frecpe + frecpx + frsqrte + fsqrt + fmov f2i + cvtf2i ... basic fp/asimd ops + aes + fmov f2i + cvtf2i
c-jia-fp-roles.value: 4x basic fp/simd+aes; 1 adds fdiv, frecpe, frecpx, frsqrte, fsqrt; 2 add fmov f2i, fcvtzs
c-jia-fp-roles.notes: Chen's per-unit list, set beside c-dj-fp-roles rather than against it.

c-jia-f2i-both.text: An FP-to-integer move occupies both an FP unit and an integer unit, reading the FP register file on the FP side and writing the integer register file on the integer side
c-jia-f2i-both.quote: fmov f2i 同时占用了浮点执行单元和整数执行单元，这主要是为了复用寄存器堆读写口

c-jia-i2f-lsu.text: An integer-to-FP move uses neither FP nor integer units, so Chen places it in the load/store units, which already write FP registers
c-jia-i2f-lsu.quote: fmov i2f 既不在浮点，也不在整数，那只能在访存了

c-jia-fdiv-fsqrt.text: Mixing FDIV and FSQRT drops to one pair every three cycles, guessed to be two pipelines in one unit competing for a register file write port
c-jia-fdiv-fsqrt.quote: fp fdiv 和 fp fsqrt 混合时，吞吐下降到 0.33 一个不太整的数字，猜测是因为它们属于同一个执行单元内的不同流水线，抢占寄存器堆写口

c-jia-taken-1.text: Branches run at 2 per cycle when not taken but only one taken branch completes per cycle
c-jia-taken-1.quote: 虽然 Br 的吞吐可以达到 2，但是每周期只能有一个 taken branch

c-jia-nop-8.text: NOPs are eliminated and never enter an ALU, so they fill the full 8-wide rate
c-jia-nop-8.quote: NOP 被 eliminate 了，不用进 ALU，可以打满 8 的发射宽度

c-jia-ice-units.text: Icestorm has three integer units (two with branch, one with MADD, MUL and CRC), two load units of which one also stores, and two FP/SIMD units of which one adds divide, square root and FP-to-integer moves
c-jia-ice-units.quote: 小结：Icestorm 的执行单元如下 ... alu + csel + mrs nzcv + madd + mul + crc ... load + store ... basic fp/asimd ops + aes + fdiv + frecpe + frecpx + frsqrte + fsqrt + fmov f2i

c-jia-sched-ls-48.text: Behind a long-latency op, 58 dependent loads or stores fit before rename stalls, 48 loads (43 stores) of them in the schedulable part, so the load/store scheduler holds 48
c-jia-sched-ls-48.quote: 指令 | 可调度 + 不可调度 | 可调度 ld | 58 | 48 st | 58 | 43

c-jia-sched-ls-unified.text: Loads and stores reach the same total but differ by 5 in the schedulable part, which Chen tentatively reads as one unified load/store scheduler with one non-scheduling queue
c-jia-sched-ls-unified.quote: load 和 store 总数一样但 Scheduler 差了 5，不确定是测试误差还是什么问题，暂且考虑为一个统一的 Scheduler 和同一个 Non Scheduling Queue
c-jia-sched-ls-unified.notes: Against the four 12-entry queues of c-mh-v1-sched-ls-split-queues.

c-jia-sched-fp-36.text: Schedulable FP, FP-to-integer move and FJCVTZS counts are 144, 72 and 36, in the 4:2:1 ratio of their throughput, so each of the four FP units has its own 36-entry scheduler
c-jia-sched-fp-36.quote: 可调度部分 fp 是 144，fmov f2i 是 72，fjcvtzs 是 36，有明显的 4:2:1 的关系 ... 因此四个执行单元前面各有一个独立的 36 entry 的 Scheduler
c-jia-sched-fp-36.notes: Against the 18 of c-mh-v1-sched-18, which holds Johnson's sizes about twice too large.

c-jia-fp-nsq.text: The FP probes find 12 non-schedulable entries ahead of the FP schedulers, guessed to be two 6-entry non-scheduling queues each serving two schedulers
c-jia-fp-nsq.quote: 不可调度部分，156-144=12，84-72=12，42-36=6，猜测有两个 Non Scheduling Queue，每个 Non Scheduling Queue 6 entry，分别对应两个 Scheduler
c-jia-fp-nsq.notes: The guess of two queues sits against the single FP dispatch buffer of c-mh-v1-dispatch-fp-single.

c-jia-sched-int-134.text: The integer schedulers hold 134 schedulable ALU entries in all
c-jia-sched-int-134.quote: 可调度部分 alu 一共是 134，其中 csel 是 64，crc/idiv/bfm 都是 28，mrs nzcv 是 50

c-jia-int-nsq-24.text: The ALU probe finds 158 minus 134, 24 non-schedulable entries ahead of the integer schedulers

c-jia-int-nsq-two.text: The first three integer units share one 12-entry non-scheduling queue and the other three share the other 12 entries
c-jia-int-nsq-two.quote: 说明前三个执行单元共享一个 12 entry 的 Non Scheduling Queue；剩下三个执行单元共享剩下的 12 entry 的 Non Scheduling Queue

c-jia-sched-int-units.text: Splitting the counts by unit gives 28 scheduler entries for the MUL, MADD and CRC unit and 14 for the ALU, CSEL and FP-move unit, with 50 shared by the two branch units and 42 by the other two
c-jia-sched-int-units.quote: alu + csel + fmov f2i: 14 entries alu + fmov f2i: y entries alu + mul + madd + crc: 28 entries alu + mul: 42-y entries
c-jia-sched-int-units.notes: Against the 13 of c-mh-v1-sched-int-13; the split of the 50 and the 42 is left open.

c-jia-ice-sched.text: On Icestorm 24 loads or stores fit with 10 schedulable loads (4 stores), and the three integer units share one 8-entry non-scheduling queue ahead of 28 schedulable ALU entries
c-jia-ice-sched.quote: ld | 24 | 10 st | 24 | 4 alu | 36 | 28 ... 应该是 3 个整数执行单元共享一个 8 entry 的 Non Scheduling Queue

c-jia-nop-window.text: Behind 21 to 26 chained FSQRTs (13 cycles each) the NOP filler stops growing near 2277, the total entries of all ROB groups
c-jia-nop-window.quote: 可以看到 N 最大在 2277 附近就不能再增加了，说明遇到了 ROB 的瓶颈，预计 ROB 的所有 group 的 entry 个数加起来大概是 2277 左右

c-jia-rob-ldst-325.text: With loads or stores as filler at most 325 are in flight, whatever the load/store queue sizes, read as one load or store per ROB group
c-jia-rob-ldst-325.quote: 如果把填充的指令改成 load/store，inflight 的 load 和 store 最多都是 325 个，并且这和 load/store queue 大小无关

c-jia-rob-side-effects.text: ROB groups limit the type and number of instructions in them so that instructions with side effects, which need special handling at retire, sit only at the start of a group
c-jia-rob-side-effects.quote: 对于有副作用的指令，retire 时是需要特殊处理的，因此一个合理的设计就是，让这些指令只能放在 group 的开头

c-jia-rob-groups.text: 2277 over 325 is close to 7, so the ROB has about 330 groups of up to 7 uops each
c-jia-rob-groups.quote: 结论：Firestorm 的 ROB 有大约 330 个 group，每个 group 最多保存 7 个 uop

c-jia-rob-group-7.text: Each ROB group holds at most 7 uops
c-jia-rob-group-7.quote: 每个 group 最多保存 7 个 uop

c-jia-chase-prefetch.text: Pointer-chase latency on Firestorm fluctuates a lot, apparently because the prefetcher is tuned for pointer chasing
c-jia-chase-prefetch.quote: 发现 Firestorm 上 pointer chasing 的延迟波动比较大，目测是 prefetcher 做了针对性的优化

c-jia-ice-rob.text: Icestorm's NOP window steps at 413 instructions and its load/store window near 57, so its ROB has 59 groups of up to 7 uops
c-jia-ice-rob.quote: 可以看到拐点是 413 条指令。改成用 load/store 指令，可以测到拐点在 57 左右 ... 结论：Icestorm 的 ROB 有 59 个 group，每个 group 最多保存 7 个 uop

c-jia-sysctl-l2.text: macOS reports a 12 MB L2 shared by the four Firestorm cores and a 4 MB L2 shared by the four Icestorm cores
c-jia-sysctl-l2.quote: 4 个 Firestorm 核心共享一个 12MB L2 Cache，4 个 Icestorm 核心共享一个 4MB L2 Cache ... hw.perflevel0.l2cachesize: 12582912 hw.perflevel0.cpusperl2: 4
c-jia-sysctl-l2.notes: macOS sysctl values as read by Chen.

c-jia-guide-l2.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the M1 and A14 P-cluster L2 as 12 MiB, 12-way, 128 B lines, and the E-cluster L2 as 4 MiB, 16-way, 128 B lines
c-jia-guide-l2.quote: M1 Family/A14 Bionic: P-Core cluster 12MiB, 12-way, 128B lines; E-Core cluster 4MiB, 16-way, 128B lines

c-jia-guide-slc-size.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the memory cache (SLC) of the M1, M2, M3 and M4 as 8 MiB
c-jia-guide-slc-size.quote: Memory Cache（在别的处理器也叫 System Level Cache，就是 Last Level Cache）的配置如下 ... M1/M2/M3/M4: 8MiB, 16-way, 128B lines

c-jia-guide-slc-ways.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the M1 memory cache 16 ways

c-jia-guide-slc-line.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the M1 memory cache 128 B lines
c-jia-guide-slc-line.notes: From Apple's optimization guide. Contradicts the mechanism's 512 B sectored line (c-mh-v8-slc-line-512).

c-jia-guide-slc-pro-max.text: Apple's optimization guide gives the memory cache as 24 MiB, 12-way on the M1 Pro, 48 MiB, 12-way on the M1 Max and 96 MiB, 12-way on the M1 Ultra, all with 128 B lines
c-jia-guide-slc-pro-max.quote: M1 Pro/M2 Pro/M4 Pro/A16 Bionic/A17 Pro/A18 Pro: 24MiB, 12-way, 128B lines ... M1 Max/M2 Max/M3 Max/M4 Max: 48MiB, 12-way, 128B lines ... M1 Ultra/M2 Ultra/M3 Ultra: 96MiB, 12-way, 128B lines
c-jia-guide-slc-pro-max.notes: From Apple's optimization guide. Values for the M1 Pro, Max and Ultra, not the M1.

c-jia-guide-l2tlb.text: Apple's optimization guide gives every P-core from the A14 and M1 to the A18 and M4 a 3072-entry L2 TLB
c-jia-guide-l2tlb.quote: P-Core 的 L2 TLB 容量，从 M1 Family 到 M4 Family，从 A14 Bionic 到 A18 Family，都是 3072 entries
c-jia-guide-l2tlb.notes: From Apple's optimization guide. The M1 E-core is given 1024 entries.

c-jia-l2tlb-unified.text: Apple's performance counters split the L1 TLBs into instruction and data while the L2 TLB serves both
c-jia-l2tlb-unified.quote: 从苹果提供的性能计数器来看，L1 TLB 分为指令和数据，而 L2 TLB 是 Unified，不区分指令和数据

c-jia-l2tlb-3072.text: Extending the page-spread pointer chase, the L2 TLB step comes at 3072 pages
c-jia-l2tlb-3072.quote: 可以看到拐点是 3072 个 Page，说明 Firestorm 的 L2 TLB 容量是 3072 项

c-jia-l2tlb-org.text: With one pointer every 32 to 256 pages the L2 TLB step falls from 96 to 12 and stays at 12 for 512, so the L2 TLB is 12-way with 256 sets indexed by VA bits 21:14
c-jia-l2tlb-org.quote: 认为 Firestorm 的 L2 TLB 是 12 Way，256 Set，Index 位是 VA[21:14]
c-jia-l2tlb-org.notes: Agrees with c-mh-v2-tlb2-256x12; against the hashed 3-way, 1024-set reading of c-mh-v2-tlb2-org.

c-jia-l2tlb-miss.text: In the page-spread chase a load takes 3 cycles on an L1 dTLB hit, 9 on an L2 TLB hit and 35 to 36.5 on an L2 TLB miss, with no cache misses
c-jia-l2tlb-miss.quote: 观察到命中 L1 DTLB 时 CPI 是 3，命中 L2 TLB 时 CPI 是 9，L2 TLB 缺失时 CPI 是 35-36.5，此时缓存缺失率为 0

c-jia-ice-l2tlb.text: Icestorm's L2 TLB holds 1024 entries and, if 4-way, has 256 sets indexed by VA bits 21:14
c-jia-ice-l2tlb.quote: 可以看到拐点是 1024 个 Page，说明 Icestorm 的 L2 TLB 容量是 1024 项 ... 假如是 4 Way，那么 Icestorm 的 L2 TLB 是 4 Way，256 Set，Index 位是 VA[21:14]

c-jc-ras-sweep.text: In Chen's call-depth sweep the minimum time per call level stays near 1.1 up to a depth of 50 and jumps to about 5.6 at 51, staying near 5 out to 64
c-jc-ras-sweep.notes: Columns are depth, min, avg and max; the unit of time is not given. The diagram labels this a 50-entry RAS.

c-jc-lq-130.text: The load sweep shows a step at 130 loads, taken as a 130-entry load queue
c-jc-lq-130.quote: load: spike at 130(pattern 4) and 188(pattern5, 188=130+48(scheduler)+10(dispatch queue)) 130-entry Load Queue

c-jc-load-188.text: A second load pattern steps at 188, which Chen splits into 130 load queue entries, 48 scheduler entries and 10 dispatch queue entries

c-jc-store-107.text: Two store patterns step at 107, which Chen reads as 60 store queue entries plus 48 scheduler entries less one

c-jc-store-118.text: A third store pattern steps at 118, which is 60 store queue entries plus 48 scheduler and 10 dispatch queue entries; the 60 is computed as 118 minus 48 minus 10
c-jc-store-118.quote: 118(pattern 7, 60+48(scheduler)+10(dispatch queue)) ... 60 was computed by 118 - 48(scheduler) - 10(dispatch queue) 60-entry Store Queue

c-jc-lsu-steps.text: In the raw store sweep, pattern 7 holds near 114 up to 118 stores and jumps to about 185 at 119; the load pattern 5 jumps between 188 and 189 in the same way
c-jc-lsu-steps.notes: Columns are pattern, size, min, avg and max; the unit of time is not given.

c-jc-sched-ls-48.text: The load/store probe fits 58 ops, 48 of them in the schedulable part, so the memory scheduler holds 48
c-jc-sched-ls-48.quote: Source: jiegec, 58(10+48) sched size for load & store ... Source: jiegec, 48 sched size for load & store

c-jc-dispatch-ls-10.text: The other 10 of the 58 load/store entries are the memory dispatch queue
c-jc-dispatch-ls-10.quote: Source: jiegec, 58(10+48) sched size for load & store ... 10-entry Memory Dispatch Queue

c-jc-int-sched-133.text: The ALU probe fits 158 ops, 133 of them schedulable, which Chen matches to two 12-entry dispatch queues and schedulers of 24, 26, 16, 12, 28 and 28 entries
c-jc-int-sched-133.quote: Source: jiegec, 158(=12+12+24+26+16+12+28+28) sched size for alu ... Source: jiegec, 133(~=134=24+26+16+12+28+28) sched w/o nsq size for alu

c-jc-mul-sched-28.text: The integer multiply probe fits 68 ops, 56 of them schedulable, matching two 28-entry schedulers behind one 12-entry dispatch queue
c-jc-mul-sched-28.quote: Source: jiegec, 68(12+28+28) sched size for imul ... Source: jiegec, 56(28+28) sched w/o nsq size for imul
c-jc-mul-sched-28.notes: Against the 13 per multiply queue of c-mh-v1-sched-int-13.

c-jc-fp-sched-36.text: The FP probe fits 156 ops, 143 of them schedulable, matching one 12-entry FP dispatch queue ahead of four 36-entry schedulers
c-jc-fp-sched-36.quote: Source: jiegec, 156(=12+36+36+36+36) sched size for fp ... Source: jiegec, 143(~=144=36+36+36+36) sched w/o nsq size for fp dispatch4: 12-entry FP Dispatch Queue
c-jc-fp-sched-36.notes: Same data as c-jia-sched-fp-36, here with one 12-entry FP queue rather than two of 6.

c-jc-rename-620.text: Chen measures about 620 for the rename history, against Johnson's 623

c-jc-ls-pipes.text: Firestorm has two load pipes, one store pipe and one load/store pipe
c-jc-ls-pipes.quote: Source: jiegec 2 Load Pipe 1 Store Pipe 1 Load/Store Pipe

c-dj-width.text: Firestorm's pipeline width is eight instructions (uops) per cycle
c-dj-width.quote: Firestorm has a pipeline width of eight instructions per cycle. Uops per cycle: 8
c-dj-width.notes: Johnson gives one pipeline width, not separate fetch/decode/rename widths. Method from #firestorm-pipeline-overview (uops counted with the RETIRE_UOP counter against the 8 uops/cycle limit).

c-dj-taken.text: Firestorm sustains one taken branch per cycle
c-dj-taken.quote: Uops per cycle: 8 Taken branches per cycle: 1
c-dj-taken.notes: The page does not say how this was measured.

c-dj-int-prf.text: The integer physical register file holds about 380 to 394 registers
c-dj-int-prf.quote: Integer physical register file size: ~380-394? ... These numbers mostly come from my M1 buffer size measuring tool
c-dj-int-prf.notes: Johnson gives the range ~380-394 with a question mark; value is the midpoint.

c-dj-fp-prf.text: The FP/SIMD physical register file holds about 432 registers
c-dj-fp-prf.quote: FP/SIMD physical register file size: ~432? ... These numbers mostly come from my M1 buffer size measuring tool

c-dj-flags-prf.text: The flags physical register file holds about 128 registers
c-dj-flags-prf.quote: Flags physical register file size: ~128 ... These numbers mostly come from my M1 buffer size measuring tool

c-dj-branches.text: About 144 branches can be in flight
c-dj-branches.quote: In-flight branches: ~144 ... These numbers mostly come from my M1 buffer size measuring tool

c-dj-loads.text: About 130 loads can be in flight
c-dj-loads.quote: In-flight loads: ~130 ... These numbers mostly come from my M1 buffer size measuring tool
c-dj-loads.notes: The page points to the load/store queue blog post for detail (see c-dj-lsq-lq-130).

c-dj-stores.text: About 60 stores can be in flight
c-dj-stores.quote: In-flight stores: ~60 These numbers mostly come from my M1 buffer size measuring tool
c-dj-stores.notes: The page points to the load/store queue blog post for detail (see c-dj-lsq-sq-60).

c-dj-retire-groups.text: The coalesced retire queue holds about 330 retire groups
c-dj-retire-groups.quote: The coalesced retire queue consists of ~330 such groups.
c-dj-retire-groups.notes: The page names no filler; the LSQ post reaches this limit with ~329 loads or stores under an FSQRT delay (c-dj-lsq-fsqrt-329). Group boundaries are c-dj-group-boundaries.

c-dj-group-size.text: A retire group may contain up to seven uops
c-dj-group-size.quote: Firestorm coalesces uops into retire groups, which all retire together. A retire group may contain up to seven uops.
c-dj-group-size.notes: Seven-uop groups are only observed for eliminated instructions (c-dj-group-issuing).

c-dj-nop-window.text: The coalesced retire queue allows an out-of-order window of over 2200 nop instructions
c-dj-nop-window.quote: This allows an out-of-order window of ... or over 2200 nop instructions.

c-dj-issuing-window.text: The coalesced retire queue allows an out-of-order window of just over 1000 contrived instructions that issue
c-dj-issuing-window.quote: This allows an out-of-order window of just over 1000 (contrived) instructions that issue

c-dj-rename-retire.text: The rename retire queue allows up to about 623 renames in flight
c-dj-rename-retire.quote: This is tracked in a separate structure, called the "rename retire queue", which allows for up to ~623 renames.
c-dj-rename-retire.notes: The every-write-needs-an-entry rule is c-dj-rename-cost. Also listed in #other-limits as "In-flight renames: ~623".

c-dj-retire-rate.text: Retirement is measured at up to eight coalesced retire queue entries per cycle
c-dj-retire-rate.quote: Retirement-rate is measured at up to eight coalesced retire queue entries per cycle
c-dj-retire-rate.notes: The page says "measured" but not how.

c-dj-rename-rate.text: Retirement is measured at up to sixteen rename retire queue entries per cycle
c-dj-rename-rate.quote: or up to sixteen rename retire queue entries per cycle
c-dj-rename-rate.notes: The page says "measured" but not how.

c-dj-int-units.text: Firestorm has six integer units (1 to 6), each with ALU and ubfm/sbfm
c-dj-int-units.quote: Integer units: 1: alu + ubfm/sbfm + flags + branch ... 6: alu + ubfm/sbfm + mul + madd + crc + bfm/extr
c-dj-int-units.notes: The page says issues are measured with SCHEDULE_UOP and per-class issue counters. Unit roles are c-dj-int-roles.

c-dj-ls-units.text: Firestorm has four load/store units handling up to 128-bit accesses: unit 7 store and AMX, unit 8 load/store and AMX, units 9 and 10 load only
c-dj-ls-units.quote: Load/store units (up to 128-bit loads and stores ... 7: store + amx 8: load/store + amx 9: load 10: load

c-dj-fp-units.text: Firestorm has four FP/SIMD units (11 to 14)
c-dj-fp-units.quote: SIMD units: 11: fp/simd 12: fp/simd 13: fp/simd + fcsel + to-gpr 14: fp/simd
c-dj-fp-units.notes: Unit roles are c-dj-fp-roles. For unit 14 the page lists reciprocal and reciprocal-square-root estimates (frecpe, frsqrte, urecpe, ursqrte), not fsqrt.

c-dj-mov-elim.text: 64-bit register moves (mov x0, x1) are usually handled by renaming; mov w0, w1, mov x0, xzr and adr/adrp are not eliminated
c-dj-mov-elim.quote: mov x0, x1 (usually handled by renaming, 64-bit version only) ... not eliminated, including adr/adrp, mov w0, w1 and mov x0, xzr

c-dj-zero-idiom.text: mov x0, #0 (and its 32-bit form) and movi v0.16b, #0 (and other types) are handled by renaming
c-dj-zero-idiom.quote: mov x0, #0 (handled by renaming, as is 32-bit version) ... movi v0.16b, #0 (handled by renaming, including other types)
c-dj-zero-idiom.notes: mov x0, xzr is not eliminated (c-dj-mov-elim).

c-dj-mov-imm.text: Immediate moves (mov x0, #imm, 32- and 64-bit, including bitwise/movz/movn aliases) are handled by renaming at most twice per eight instructions
c-dj-mov-imm.quote: mov x0, #123 (handled by renaming at a max of 2 per 8 instructions, both 32-bit and 64-bit. Includes all tested immediate "mov" aliases e.g. bitwise/movz/movn)

c-dj-fusion.text: Certain consecutive instruction pairs issue as one uop: flag-setting ALU + b.cc, ALU + cbz/cbnz, aese + aesmc, aesd + aesimc, aese/aesd + eor, pmull + eor, and amx + amx
c-dj-fusion.quote: Certain instructions are able to issue as one uop if they appear consecutively in the instruction stream.
c-dj-fusion.value: flag-ALU+b.cc, ALU+cbz/cbnz, aese+aesmc, aesd+aesimc, aes+eor, pmull+eor, amx+amx
c-dj-fusion.notes: Conditions and non-fused pairs: c-dj-fusion-read-limit, c-dj-fusion-cbz, c-dj-fusion-crypto, c-dj-fusion-amx, c-dj-fusion-branch-limits and c-dj-no-fusion.

c-dj-l1d-latency.text: A load's result can feed the base address of another load with 3-cycle latency
c-dj-l1d-latency.quote: Loads may be passed to the base address of other loads with 3c latency (which is nice for linked lists)
c-dj-l1d-latency.notes: The 4c ALU-chain latency is c-dj-load-alu-latency. The page gives no method for latencies.

c-dj-pipeline-flow.text: Instructions decode to one or more uops, which are mapped, renamed and placed in a dispatch queue, then dispatched to a scheduler, issue when their operands are ready, and are marked completed in the reorder buffer, which releases entries in order
c-dj-pipeline-flow.quote: Typically, an instruction is decoded to one or more uops, each uop is mapped and renamed and placed into a dispatch queue. These uops are then dispatched from the queue to a scheduler.

c-dj-issue-counters.text: Issues are counted by the documented SCHEDULE_UOP counter, and three undocumented counters count issues to the integer, load/store and SIMD units separately; uops are counted by RETIRE_UOP
c-dj-issue-counters.quote: can be measured using the documented SCHEDULE_UOP counter. Three undocumented counters measure issues to the integer, load/store, and simd units separately

c-dj-unit-issue-limit.text: Each execution unit accepts one issue per cycle
c-dj-unit-issue-limit.quote: Issues count towards the "execution unit" limits (one issue per unit per cycle)

c-dj-fewer-issues.text: Most instructions issue once per uop, but nop, ldp and fused instructions have fewer issues than uops
c-dj-fewer-issues.quote: most instructions have the same number of issues as uops, but some have fewer (e.g. nop, ldp, and fused instructions)

c-dj-shift-extend-issues.text: ALU operations with an optional shift or extend have more issues than uops
c-dj-shift-extend-issues.quote: some instructions have more issues than uops, e.g ALU operations with an optional shift or extend

c-dj-issue-peak.text: Because shifted/extended ALU ops issue more than once per uop, Firestorm can sustain 11 issues per cycle in contrived cases
c-dj-issue-peak.quote: which allows Firestorm to sustain 11 issues per cycle in contrived cases

c-dj-int-roles.text: All six integer units do ALU and ubfm/sbfm; units 1-3 set flags; 1 and 2 take branches, adr and msr/mrs nzcv; 1 also mrs; 2 indirect branches and pointer authentication; 3 and 4 probably moves from SIMD/FP; 5 and 6 multiply; 5 divide; 6 madd, crc and bfm/extr
c-dj-int-roles.quote: 1: alu + ubfm/sbfm + flags + branch ... indirect branch + ptrauth ... mov-from-simd/fp? ... 5: alu + ubfm/sbfm + mul + div 6: ... mul + madd + crc + bfm/extr
c-dj-int-roles.value: 1-6 alu, ubfm/sbfm; 1-3 flags; 1-2 branch, adr, msr/mrs nzcv; 1 mrs; 2 indirect branch, ptrauth; 3-4 mov-from-simd/fp?; 5-6 mul; 5 div; 6 madd, crc, bfm/extr

c-dj-fp-roles.text: All four SIMD units do FP/SIMD; units 13 and 14 add fcsel and moves to GPRs; unit 14 alone adds fcmp/fcmpe, fdiv, frecpe, frsqrte, fjcvtzs, ursqrte, urecpe and sha
c-dj-fp-roles.quote: 13: fp/simd + fcsel + to-gpr 14: fp/simd + fcsel + to-gpr + fcmp/e + fdiv + frecpe + frsqrte + fjcvtzs + ursqrte + urecpe + sha
c-dj-fp-roles.value: 11-14 fp/simd; 13-14 fcsel, to-gpr; 14 fcmp/e, fdiv, frecpe, frsqrte, fjcvtzs, ursqrte, urecpe, sha

c-dj-agu-shift.text: Load/store address generation includes register shifts up to LSL #3
c-dj-agu-shift.quote: Load/store units (up to 128-bit loads and stores, including address generation with shifts up to LSL #3)

c-dj-fusion-read-limit.text: Flag-setting ALU ops (adds/subs/ands/cmp/tst) fuse with a following b.cc; fusion is complete only when the fused instructions read no more than 4 registers per 6 instructions
c-dj-fusion-read-limit.quote: adds/subs/ands/cmp/tst + b.cc (complete fusion when fused instructions read no more than 4 registers per 6 instructions)

c-dj-fusion-cbz.text: ALU ops (add/sub/and/orr/eor/bic etc., including flag-setting variants) usually fuse with a following cbz/cbnz when their destination is the cbz operand
c-dj-fusion-cbz.quote: add/sub/and/orr/eor/bic/etc. + cbnz/cbz (usually fused, if destination matches cbz operand. also works with instruction variants that set flags)

c-dj-fusion-crypto.text: aese + aesmc, aesd + aesimc, aese/aesd + eor and pmull + eor usually fuse when the second instruction overwrites the first's destination in a matching operand pattern
c-dj-fusion-crypto.quote: aese + aesmc (usually fused if operands match pattern "A, B ; A, A") ... pmull + eor (usually fused if operands match pattern "A, B, C ; A, A, D" or "A, B, C ; A, D, A")

c-dj-fusion-amx.text: Pairs of AMX instructions fuse, except AMX loads and stores, probably into something like an stp
c-dj-fusion-amx.quote: amx + amx (excluding loads and stores - probably fuses to something like a stp)

c-dj-fusion-branch-limits.text: Branch fusion does not happen with implicit shift or extend, nor with instructions that read flags such as adc
c-dj-fusion-branch-limits.quote: Branch fusion does not work with implicit shift or extend, nor instructions that read flags (like adc)

c-dj-no-fusion.text: adrp + add, mov + movk, mul + umulh and udiv + msub are not fused
c-dj-no-fusion.quote: Other tested patterns are not fused, including adrp + add, mov + movk, mul + umulh, and udiv + msub.

c-dj-vec-mov-elim.text: Full-width vector register moves (mov v0.16b, v1.16b, also v0.8h etc.) are usually handled by renaming; v0.8b moves are not
c-dj-vec-mov-elim.quote: mov v0.16b, v1.16b (usually handled by renaming. Includes other full-width types e.g. v0.8h but not v0.8b)

c-dj-nop-b-no-issue.text: nop and unconditional b never issue
c-dj-nop-b-no-issue.quote: Certain instructions do not need to issue: ... nop (never issues) b (unconditional branch never issues)

c-dj-load-alu-latency.text: When a load is chained with ALU operations instead of feeding another load's base address, its latency is 4 cycles
c-dj-load-alu-latency.quote: Loads may be passed to the base address of other loads with 3c latency ... but chaining with ALU operations gives a latency of 4c.

c-dj-ldp-second-dest.text: The second destination register of an LDP always has 4-cycle latency
c-dj-ldp-second-dest.quote: (Although the second destination register in an LDP always has 4c latency.)

c-dj-index-shift-penalty.text: A load takes one extra cycle when its index register comes from a shift-like instruction; addition and bitwise producers carry no penalty
c-dj-index-shift-penalty.quote: Loads may have an extra 1-cycle of latency when the index register is the output of a shift-like instruction. Addition and bitwise operations do not have this penalty.
c-dj-index-shift-penalty.notes: Johnson says other latency chains had not been tested.

c-dj-madd-acc-latency.text: A MADD result feeds the addend of a following MADD with 1-cycle latency, but has 3-cycle latency into other instructions
c-dj-madd-acc-latency.quote: MADD's output can be passed to its third operand (the addend) with 1c latency, but if it's chained with other instructions it has 3c latency.

c-dj-int-simd-roundtrip.text: An integer-to-SIMD/FP-and-back round trip can take as little as 7 cycles, for example when chaining flags operations
c-dj-int-simd-roundtrip.quote: Integer to SIMD/FP roundtrip latency can be as low as 7c (e.g. when chaining flags operations).

c-dj-rob-model.text: Firestorm's reorder buffer is unconventional: a ~330-entry coalesced retire queue of retire groups plus a ~623-entry rename retire queue
c-dj-rob-model.quote: Firestorm uses an unconventional reorder buffer, which I described as a ~330 entry "coalesced retire queue" and a ~623 "rename retire queue"
c-dj-rob-model.value: coalesced retire queue + rename retire queue

c-dj-reclaim-table.text: Johnson equates the ~623-entry rename retire queue with a Physical Register Reclaim Table
c-dj-reclaim-table.quote: a ~623 "rename retire queue" (equivalent to a "Physical Register Reclaim Table")

c-dj-group-boundaries.text: Uops that can fail before retiring (such as memory accesses) must start a retire group, and uops that can fail after retiring (such as conditional branches) must end one
c-dj-group-boundaries.quote: Uops which can fail before retiring (such as memory accesses) must appear at the start of a group, and uops that can fail after retiring (such as conditional branches) must appear at the end of a group.

c-dj-ooo-commit.text: Non-speculative loads and stores may commit out of order, before retirement; once a store has completed, the architectural state must have advanced past it
c-dj-ooo-commit.quote: loads and stores may commit out-of-order if they are non-speculative. This has some interesting implications. In particular, once a store has "completed", the architectural state must have advanced past that point.
c-dj-ooo-commit.notes: Johnson refers to his load/store queue blog post for the evidence.

c-dj-lsq-alloc-issue.text: Load and store queue entries are allocated when the ops issue from the scheduler, not at rename or dispatch
c-dj-lsq-alloc-issue.quote: discovered that load and store queue entries are allocated when the ops issue from the scheduler
c-dj-lsq-alloc-issue.notes: Intro, before the first heading. Reasoning in #final-notes: the 58-instruction gap between loads+loads and fsqrts+loads means loads keep entering the scheduler after the queue is full, "So I conclude that the resources are allocated late."

c-dj-lsq-lq-130.text: With two cache-missing loads as the delay, 128 loads fit between them before a stall; counting both delay loads, the load queue holds 130 entries
c-dj-lsq-lq-130.quote: Since the first load, 128 other loads, and the last load are in flight at the same time, I'd call this a load queue size of 130
c-dj-lsq-lq-130.notes: Delay: two independent cache-missing loads; filler: loads. Johnson: "I still believe this to be correct". The FSQRT + dependent-branch probe gives 188 = 130 + 58 (c-dj-lsq-branch-loads-188).

c-dj-lsq-store-107.text: With cache-missing loads as the delay, 107 stores fit between them before a stall; Johnson withdrew his earlier reading of this as a 107-entry store queue
c-dj-lsq-store-107.quote: 128 loads or 107 stores could run, without stopping the final long-latency load from executing in parallel ... I incorrectly called this a 107 entry store queue.
c-dj-lsq-store-107.notes: Delay: two cache-missing loads; filler: stores. Explained as 60 store-queue entries plus 47 scheduler entries (c-dj-lsq-scheduler-47); the base-register effect is c-dj-lsq-x29-base.

c-dj-lsq-sched-48.quote: the load/store scheduler has 48 entries ... I found the last point at which an independent load could still fit into the scheduler and run, to find the scheduler size.
c-dj-lsq-sched-48.filler: loads or stores with addresses dependent on the delay
c-dj-lsq-sched-48.notes: Delay: a long-latency chain; filler: loads or stores whose addresses depend on it; probe: one independent load that still runs. Repeated in #fighting-stores-with-square-roots.

c-dj-lsq-dispatch-10.text: The load/store dispatch queue in front of the scheduler has 10 entries
c-dj-lsq-dispatch-10.quote: with a 10 entry dispatch queue ... the number of extra load/stores, once the scheduler was full, that were required to block independent floating-point operations. That gives the dispatch queue size.
c-dj-lsq-dispatch-10.filler: loads or stores with addresses dependent on the delay
c-dj-lsq-dispatch-10.notes: Delay: a long-latency chain; filler: dependent loads/stores beyond a full scheduler; probe: independent FP ops that get blocked. Mixing op types separates the queues.

c-dj-lsq-dispatch-stall.text: An op that finds both its scheduler and its dispatch queue full stalls the frontend: no further ops enter any dispatch queue until that queue has room
c-dj-lsq-dispatch-stall.quote: But if the scheduler and dispatch queue are full, and we have an op that needs to go to that queue, we stall. This means no more ops can enter any dispatch queues until there is room in that queue.

c-dj-lsq-fsqrt-329.text: With chains of square roots as the delay, about 329 loads or stores fit between them, the same limit for mixed loads and stores; Johnson attributes it to the coalescing retire queue, not the load/store queues
c-dj-lsq-fsqrt-329.quote: about 329 loads or stores can run between floating point operations, without forcing the two long-latency chains to run completely in parallel
c-dj-lsq-fsqrt-329.notes: Delay: long-latency FP chains (fsqrt, per the heading and #final-notes); filler: independent loads or stores. Exceeds the 130/60 queue sizes, so queue entries are freed before retirement (c-dj-lsq-release-nonspec).

c-dj-lsq-release-nonspec.text: Loads and stores complete, freeing their load/store queue entries but not their retire queue entries, once they are non-speculative
c-dj-lsq-release-nonspec.quote: I'm guessing that loads and stores can complete (free their load/store queue entries, but not their retire queue entries) once they are non-speculative.
c-dj-lsq-release-nonspec.notes: Tested by making the loads/stores speculative: one initial load/store whose address depends on the delay, or (in the write-up) a branch dependent on it (c-dj-lsq-branch-loads-188).

c-dj-lsq-release-in-order.text: Load/store completion that frees queue entries happens in order relative to other loads and stores
c-dj-lsq-release-in-order.quote: I believe this completion is in-order relative to other loads and stores.
c-dj-lsq-release-in-order.notes: The intro states it as entries "released once they are non-speculative and all earlier loads and stores have been released".

c-dj-lsq-branch-loads-188.text: With a square-root delay and a branch dependent on it keeping the loads speculative, 188 loads fit before a stall
c-dj-lsq-branch-loads-188.quote: adding a branch, dependent on the result of the first long-latency operation ... we can run 188 loads or 118 stores without forcing the two long-latency chains to run completely in parallel
c-dj-lsq-branch-loads-188.notes: Delay: FSQRT chain plus a dependent B.cc (chained via FCMP, per #the-data, since FMOV might interfere); filler: loads. 188 = 130 queue + 48 scheduler + 10 dispatch queue.

c-dj-lsq-branch-stores-118.text: With a square-root delay and a branch dependent on it keeping the stores speculative, 118 stores fit before a stall
c-dj-lsq-branch-stores-118.quote: This will ensure the loads and stores cannot become non-speculative, and keep their queue entries. In this test we see we can run 188 loads or 118 stores
c-dj-lsq-branch-stores-118.notes: Delay: FSQRT chain plus a dependent B.cc (chained via FCMP); filler: stores. 118 = 60 store queue + 58.

c-dj-lsq-extra-58.text: The 58 entries beyond the queue sizes are the 48-entry load/store scheduler plus its 10-entry dispatch queue: integer and FP work continues while they fill, and the next load/store stalls the machine
c-dj-lsq-extra-58.quote: If the load/store scheduler and dispatch queue are full, the integer and floating point units can continue operating. But if we hit one more load/store, the machine stalls ... This explains the 58 extra entries.

c-dj-lsq-sq-60.text: Subtracting the 58 scheduler and dispatch-queue entries from the 118-store result, the store queue has 60 entries
c-dj-lsq-sq-60.quote: By this logic (subtracting 58 for the size of the scheduler and dispatch queue), the store queue has only 60 entries.
c-dj-lsq-sq-60.notes: Delay: FSQRT chain plus a dependent branch; filler: stores; 118 - 58. Johnson's summary: "130 load queue entries and 60 store queue entries".

c-dj-lsq-scheduler-47.text: The earlier 107-store result is 60 store-queue entries plus 47: a probe load can still enter and issue while the 48-entry scheduler has one free entry, but not once it is full
c-dj-lsq-scheduler-47.quote: So why did we think it had 47 more? Because if the 48 entry scheduler is almost full, but has one free entry, then a load can enter the scheduler, and then issue from the scheduler and execute

c-dj-lsq-x29-base.text: With cache-missing loads as the delay, the store probe gives 60 when the second delay load is based on X29 and the stores on X29 or SP, but 107 when either base register is X3 (same values)
c-dj-lsq-x29-base.quote: I tried to reproduce the "107 entry store queue" result, but the result I got was 60 entries ... Changing either or both registers back to X3 (even though the values did not change) gave me 107 again.
c-dj-lsq-x29-base.hedge: take this section with a grain of salt
c-dj-lsq-x29-base.notes: Delay: two cache-missing loads (second one X29 + variable offset); filler: stores at X29 or SP + constant offset. In a July 2022 update Johnson could not reproduce this section on an M1 Max and suspects hardware or software revisions.

c-dj-lsq-x29-prediction.text: Memory dependency prediction appears to special-case X29 (the frame pointer): the load waits until it knows no older store aliases it, which it can check for up to 60 speculative stores but not 61
c-dj-lsq-x29-prediction.quote: X29 is typically used as the stack frame base pointer, and I suspect the memory dependency prediction has a special case for this, and makes the load wait until it knows the store doesn't alias it.
c-dj-lsq-x29-prediction.notes: Same M1 Max non-reproduction caveat as c-dj-lsq-x29-base. The intro calls it "a trick for manipulating load/store alias prediction".

c-dj-lsq-mov-counter.text: Apple's PMU has a MEMORY_ORDER_VIOLATION event, described as incorrect speculation between a store and a dependent load
c-dj-lsq-mov-counter.quote: Apple provides a performance counter for this. It's called MEMORY_ORDER_VIOLATION and described as "Incorrect speculation between store and dependent load".

c-dj-lsq-prf-not-late.text: Physical register file probes show no delay-type dependence (int+int vs int+float), so registers are neither allocated late nor freed early
c-dj-lsq-prf-not-late.quote: I do not see this kind of pattern when measuring physical register file sizes (e.g. comparing int+int vs int+float), so I believe they are neither allocated late, nor freed early.

c-dj-ice-lq-30.quote: The same logic works for Icestorm, where we see 30 load queue entries and 18 store queue entries

c-dj-ice-sq-18.quote: The same logic works for Icestorm, where we see 30 load queue entries and 18 store queue entries
c-dj-ice-sq-18.notes: The X29-based probe also measures 18 on Icestorm (#an-uncomfortable-surprising-discovery).

c-dj-ice-sched-ls-18.quote: 18 store queue entries (with an 18 entry scheduler and a 6 entry dispatch queue)

c-dj-ice-dispatch-ls-6.text: Icestorm's load/store dispatch queue has 6 entries
c-dj-ice-dispatch-ls-6.quote: with an 18 entry scheduler and a 6 entry dispatch queue

c-dj-group-issuing.text: Groups of seven uops are only observed for eliminated instructions; issuing uops are limited to roughly four per retire group
c-dj-group-issuing.quote: with issuing uops limited to roughly four per group
c-dj-group-issuing.notes: 330 groups at four issuing uops is ~1,320, not the "just over 1000" issuing window the same paragraph gives; three per group (~990) fits that window

c-dj-rename-cost.text: Every architectural register write takes a rename retire queue entry, eliminated or not: cbz and str take none, add and mov one, adds and ldp two
c-dj-rename-cost.quote: cbz or str do not require entries, add and mov need one entry, and adds or ldp need two entries

c-keeter-ret-mismatch.text: A loop entered once by BL and left by a RET on every iteration, so the returns never match calls, runs about four times slower than the same work with a matched BL and RET per iteration
c-keeter-ret-mismatch.quote: The "optimized" code with one jump per loop is about 4x slower than the original version with two jumps per loop!
c-keeter-ret-mismatch.notes: Measured on an M1 Max over a 1024-element array, 969 ns against 3.85 us. Every RET in the loop goes to the same address.

c-keeter-ret-mispredict.text: With mismatched calls and returns the return-mispredict counter reads about 929 million over 1 billion iterations against 92 with matched pairs, so about 93% of returns are mispredicted
c-keeter-ret-mispredict.quote: BRANCH_RET_INDIR_MISPRED_NONSPECIFIC | 92 | 928,644,975 ... with mismatched bl / ret pairs, the return branch predictor fails about 93% of the time
c-keeter-ret-mispredict.notes: Measured on an M1 Max, summing a 1 billion element array.

c-keeter-br-x30.text: Replacing each RET with BR X30, which does not mark a return, removes the slowdown: 913 ns against 969 ns for matched pairs
c-keeter-br-x30.quote: Dan made the great suggestion of replacing ret with br x30 to test this theory. Sure enough, this fixes the performance regression ... One bl , many br x30 | 913 ns
c-keeter-br-x30.notes: Measured on an M1 Max. Keeter puts the small gain over matched pairs down to one branch per iteration instead of two.

c-keeter-ras-model.text: Keeter reads the result as a return stack pushed by every BL and popped by every RET, which predicts a RET to the most recent BL and fails when many RETs share one call
c-keeter-ras-model.quote: the branch predictor probably keeps an internal stack of function return addresses, which is pushed to whenever a bl is executed
c-keeter-ras-model.notes: Every RET in the loop goes to the same address, yet most are mispredicted (c-keeter-ret-mispredict).

c-keeter-restart-counters.text: With mismatched returns FETCH_RESTART rises from about 61 thousand to 988 million, MAP_DISPATCH_BUBBLE from 1.2 to 7.4 billion and MAP_REWIND from 6.4 million to 2.8 billion over 1 billion iterations
c-keeter-restart-counters.notes: Measured on an M1 Max. Keeter guesses these are downstream effects of the mispredicted returns.

c-lem-m1-mlp-28.text: One M1 core keeps about 28 random memory accesses in flight at once, possibly more
c-lem-m1-mlp-28.quote: It looks like a single core has about 28 levels of memory parallelism ... and possibly more.
c-lem-m1-mlp-28.hedge: It looks like ... and possibly more
c-lem-m1-mlp-28.notes: A lower bound on misses in flight beyond the L1D from one core, not an L1D miss-buffer count (mshr.outstanding). The test is not described here; his lane test stops at 28 lanes (c-lem-m2-lanes).

c-lem-m1-adjacent.text: In random byte gathers over a 1 GB array, also reading the byte after each address makes a 2-wise gather 40% slower, 8.9 to 12.5 ns per iteration, close to a 3-wise gather at 13.0 ns, so a second access next to a random one is not free
c-lem-m1-adjacent.quote: 2-wise | 8.9 ns ... 2-wise + | 12.5 ns ... the last one is 40% more expensive than the first 2-wise function. It contradicts our prediction.
c-lem-m1-adjacent.hedge: The run-to-run variability is relatively high on such a test
c-lem-m1-adjacent.notes: He gives no cause; the extra reads target the byte after each random address.

c-lem-m2-lanes.text: Split into lanes, a random pointer chase over an array of over 33 million 64-bit words shows one M2 core visibly sustaining 28 lanes, the most the test runs because more lanes are too noisy
c-lem-m2-lanes.quote: I have to limit the number of lanes since beyond a certain point, there is too much noise. A maximum of 28 lanes works well. ... Both processors can visibly sustain 28 lanes.
c-lem-m2-lanes.hedge: I have to limit the number of lanes since beyond a certain point, there is too much noise
c-lem-m2-lanes.notes: A floor, not a limit, since the test stops at 28 lanes. Same figure as the M1 (c-lem-m1-mlp-28).

c-lem-m4-lanes.text: One M4 core also sustains the full 28 lanes and runs the test only about 15% faster than the M2
c-lem-m4-lanes.quote: the difference between the M4 and the M2 is not enormous (about 15%). Both processors can visibly sustain 28 lanes.
c-lem-m4-lanes.notes: The M4 uses LPDDR5X memory, the M2 LPDDR5. The test stops at 28 lanes.

c-lx-dcs-eight.text: The M1's power-domain tree has eight DCS domains, each an LPDDR4 interface, beside a single MCC memory-controller domain
c-lx-dcs-eight.quote: label = "mcc"; apple,always-on; /* Memory controller */ ... label = "dcs7"; apple,always-on; /* LPDDR4 interface */
c-lx-dcs-eight.notes: Domains dcs0 to dcs7, all kept on by Linux. Matches eight 16-bit channels in c-7cpu-memory; how addresses spread over them is not stated.

c-lx-fabric-critical.text: Two fabric blocks of the M1, IMX and SMX, are kept on as critical blocks in its power-domain tree, with APCIe hanging off IMX
c-lx-fabric-critical.quote: label = "imx"; apple,always-on; /* Apple fabric, critical block */ ... label = "smx"; apple,always-on; /* Apple fabric, critical block */ ... power-domains = <&ps_imx>, <&ps_pcie_ref>;
c-lx-fabric-critical.notes: The source does not say which traffic each block carries.

c-lx-fabric-powerdown.text: Two other fabric blocks of the M1 can power down, RMX for display and image clients and MMX for media clients
c-lx-fabric-powerdown.quote: label = "rmx"; /* Apple Fabric, display/image stuff: this can power down */ ... label = "mmx"; /* Apple Fabric, media stuff: this can power down */
c-lx-fabric-powerdown.notes: In the tree the ISP and display front ends hang off RMX, and the video encoder, decoder and JPEG blocks off MMX.

c-lx-aic-v1.text: The M1's AIC (version 1) gives each hardware IRQ one mask bit and a per-IRQ target, delivers through one event/ack register per CPU with lower IRQ numbers first, and masks an IRQ when its event is read
c-lx-aic-v1.quote: - Single mask bit per IRQ * - Per-IRQ affinity setting * - Automatic masking on event delivery (auto-ack) ... - Automatic prioritization (single event/ack register per CPU, lower IRQs = * higher priority)
c-lx-aic-v1.notes: The driver binds the T8103 to AIC version 1 and sets one target CPU per IRQ; it shows no cluster-by-cluster offering.

c-lx-fiq.text: On the M1, FIQs come from fast IPIs, the four Arm timers and the per-core and per-cluster performance counters rather than through the AIC
c-lx-fiq.quote: - Fast IPIs (not yet used) * - The 4 timers (CNTP, CNTV for each of HV and guest) * - Per-core PMCs (not yet supported) * - Per-cluster uncore PMCs (not yet supported)
c-lx-fiq.notes: No register gives the FIQ source, so the driver checks each source in turn.

c-lx-local-ipi.text: From the M1 on, a fast IPI to a core in the sender's cluster goes through the local request register, and one to another cluster through the global register with a cluster field
c-lx-local-ipi.quote: /* True if SYS_IMP_APL_IPI_RR_LOCAL_EL1 exists for local fast IPIs (M1+) */ ... if (static_branch_likely(&use_local_fast_ipi) && MPIDR_CLUSTER(my_mpidr) == cluster) { write_sysreg_s(FIELD_PREP(IPI_RR_CPU, idx), SYS_IMP_APL_IPI_RR_LOCAL_EL1);
