c-tso-l1-virt-indexed.notes: Cites the S2C paper on the M1.

c-tso-m1-simd.text: On the M1 P core, cache-hitting loads of more than 16 bytes run over 10x slower in TSO mode than in Arm mode; loads of 16 bytes or less are not slowed
c-tso-m1-simd.quote: On the M1 P core TSO mode, loads of > 16 𝐵 are more than 10× slower than in Arm mode, whereas loads of ≤ 16 𝐵 are not slowed down.
c-tso-m1-simd.notes: Loops of 100 M cache-hitting loads of each ldr, ldp and ld1-ld4 variant; 10x is a lower bound.

c-tso-m4-simd.text: On the M4 P core every load variant has the same throughput in TSO and Arm modes
c-tso-m4-simd.quote: In contrast, on the M4, all loads variants have equal throughput in both modes.
c-tso-m4-simd.notes: The M1 slowdown for loads over 16 bytes (c-tso-m1-simd) is gone on the M4.

c-tso-m1-ffmpeg.text: On M1 P cores ffmpeg_x264 runs 25 % slower in TSO mode on one core and about 10 % slower on four, mostly from NEON loads of 32 bytes or more
c-tso-m1-ffmpeg.quote: Finally, on M1 P cores, ffmpeg_x264 slows down by 25% in single-core execution and by about 10% in multi-core execution.
c-tso-m1-ffmpeg.notes: Replacing each 32 B vector load with two 16 B loads removes much of the slowdown.

c-tso-m1-stl.text: On M1 P and E cores, as on the M4 P core, a load that needs more bytes than the forwarding store holds runs much slower in TSO mode than in Arm mode
c-tso-m1-stl.quote: on an M4 P core. (M1 P and E core results are qualitatively identical.)
c-tso-m1-stl.notes: The M4 P-core gap is about 5x (c-tso-stl-5x); M1 numbers are not given.

c-tso-stl-5x.text: In TSO mode store-to-load forwarding is as fast as in Arm mode when the load takes all its bytes from the store, and about 5x slower when it must also read the cache
c-tso-stl-5x.quote: STL forwarding in TSO mode is as fast as Arm’s if the load obtains all its data from the store ... but is about 5× slower otherwise, when the load must also access the cache.
c-tso-stl-5x.notes: Loops of 100 M same-address store/load pairs with 4- and 8-byte widths on an M4 P core.

c-tso-stl-dsb.text: With a DSB after each store/load pair, every width combination runs at about the same rate in both modes
c-tso-stl-dsb.quote: However, when the STL pairs are serialized by a dsb, all patterns exhibit roughly the same throughput in both modes
c-tso-stl-dsb.notes: That common rate is close to the TSO-mode rate of an 8-byte load from a 4-byte store.

c-tso-stl-serial.text: The authors hypothesize that TSO mode handles partial forwarding pairs one at a time, perhaps waiting for the store to reach the L1, though TSO does not require it
c-tso-stl-serial.quote: We therefore hypothesize that TSO mode serializes partial STL pair handling, possibly because it waits for the store to write to the L1 cache in this case (i.e., disables STL forwarding).
c-tso-stl-serial.notes: Root cause of a 70 % TSO slowdown in fluidanimate built at -O0.

c-tso-ll-reorder.text: In TSO mode the M4 still executes independent loads out of order, with the same timing as Arm mode
c-tso-ll-reorder.quote: The pattern’s execution time is identical in Arm and TSO modes, implying that TSO mode executes the loads out of order as in Arm mode.
c-tso-ll-reorder.notes: Each pattern run 1 M times between serializing barriers on M4 P cores; E-core results qualitatively the same.

c-tso-ll-violation.text: With conflicting writes from another core, Arm mode shows TSO-violating results in 99.93 % of runs, while TSO mode runs slower, consistent with squash and re-execution
c-tso-ll-violation.quote: In Arm mode, this results in observable TSO violations (determined by inspecting the values read by the loads) in 99.93% of the executions.

c-tso-ll-precise.text: A lone load whose line is invalidated before it commits, or loads forced into order, run as fast in TSO mode as in Arm mode on the M4, where Intel cores squash
c-tso-ll-precise.quote: The pattern executes with identical timing in the M4 TSO and Arm modes, but incurs TSO violation squashes on the Intel CPU.
c-tso-ll-precise.notes: Compared with Sapphire Rapids memory-ordering machine clears.

c-tso-ll-squash-rule.text: TSO mode speculatively reorders loads and squashes a load that ran out of order only if its line is invalidated from the L1 before it commits
c-tso-ll-squash-rule.quote: Load–load findings: Apple silicon TSO mode speculatively reorders loads, squashing a load that had executed out of order if its data gets invalidated from the L1 cache.
c-tso-ll-squash-rule.notes: Drawn from M4 timing patterns. Matches the load poison-bit patent Handley describes (c-mh-v3-load-poison).

c-tso-ss-hits.text: Bursts of stores to one L1-resident address run at about two stores per cycle in both modes up to 72 stores, then one per cycle
c-tso-ss-hits.quote: Both modes commit about two stores per cycle up to 𝑆 = 72
c-tso-ss-hits.notes: M4 P core. The drop past 72 matches the M4's reported 72-entry store queue.

c-tso-ss-miss-36.text: Bursts of L2-missing stores keep the same rate in both modes up to 36 stores; beyond that TSO mode falls to 0.007 stores per cycle and Arm mode to 0.05, about 7x apart
c-tso-ss-miss-36.quote: Both modes maintain equal throughput up to 𝑆 = 36. Beyond this point, their throughput diverges: TSO mode throughput converges to 0.007 stores per cycle and Arm mode to 0.05 stores per cycle
c-tso-ss-miss-36.notes: M4 P core, stores to random lines of a 64 MB buffer.

c-tso-ss-mshr-fifo.text: The authors read the 36-store knee as 36 store-miss MSHRs, each freed when its store is performed, so TSO mode frees them in order and blocks behind the oldest miss
c-tso-ss-mshr-fifo.quote: This behavior is consistent with the P core being able to sustain 36 concurrent store misses, with a miss handling register (MSHR) released once the initiating store is performed
c-tso-ss-mshr-fifo.notes: M4 P core; mshr.outstanding is still a hole for the M1.

c-tso-ss-mix.text: Placing each L2-missing store between two L1-hitting stores speeds TSO mode up 12x against 2.93x for Arm mode, so TSO mode matches Arm mode up to 80-store bursts
c-tso-ss-mix.quote: while Arm mode throughput indeed improves by up to 2.93×, TSO mode achieves a 12× improvement. It thus matches Arm mode’s throughput up to 𝑆 = 80
c-tso-ss-mix.notes: M4 P core; beyond 80 stores TSO mode falls short by at most 33 %.

c-tso-ss-reorder.text: The authors hypothesize the M4 P core performs L1-hitting stores ahead of older L2-missing stores even in TSO mode, packing more misses into the store buffer
c-tso-ss-reorder.quote: We hypothesize that the CPU performs L1-hitting stores out of order, ahead of older L2-missing stores, which increases the density of L2-missing stores in the store buffer

c-tso-ss-remote.text: When another core reads both store targets, TSO-mode store throughput drops 3x on average and up to 5x, against 16 % in Arm mode, as if the reordering is switched off
c-tso-ss-remote.quote: In contrast, TSO mode’s throughput degrades by a more severe harmonic mean of 3× and, for large values of 𝑆, by as much as 5×.
c-tso-ss-remote.notes: A remote reader of only one target has no effect, and less frequent remote reads shrink the loss.

c-tso-ss-nonspec.text: The authors suspect the store reordering is non-speculative, and it appears to reorder only L1-hitting stores
c-tso-ss-nonspec.quote: Because there is no public information on Apple silicon utilizing post-commit speculation, we suspect that it uses a non-speculative mechanism for store reordering.

c-tso-ecore-ss.text: M4 E cores show no store reordering in TSO mode: L1-hitting bursts match Arm mode, but every other store pattern runs at half the Arm-mode rate
c-tso-ecore-ss.quote: On the E cores, our experiments do not find evidence for store–store reordering. ... for all patterns, Arm mode throughput is consistently 2× better than TSO mode’s.
c-tso-ecore-ss.notes: M4 E cores. This explains the 2x TSO slowdown of lbm on M4 E cores.

c-tso-mlp-8.text: TSO-mode load throughput falls below Arm mode once a burst of loads touches more than 8 addresses with the same intra-page offset, the L1D associativity
c-tso-mlp-8.quote: TSO mode throughput drops relative to Arm mode once the load burst accesses more than 8 addresses ... exactly the associativity of the L1 data cache (see Table 1).
c-tso-mlp-8.notes: M4 P cores, E cores similar. With random intra-page offsets TSO mode matches Arm mode.

c-tso-mlp-squash.text: Out-of-order loads squashed when L1 set conflicts evict their lines limit memory-level parallelism in TSO mode and cause the large slowdowns of bwaves, cactuBSSN, wrf and roms
c-tso-mlp-squash.quote: Our analysis reveals that this effect is the root cause of the severe TSO slowdowns in bwaves, cactuBSSN, wrf, and roms.
c-tso-mlp-squash.notes: Randomizing the intra-page offset of large allocations removes these slowdowns and speeds Arm mode up too.

c-tso-cactu-misses.text: In TSO mode cactuBSSN has 50 % more L1 load misses than in Arm mode, 71 % of them from loads later squashed
c-tso-cactu-misses.quote: show that the slowdown is correlated with 50% more L1 load misses, 71% of which are due to loads that are eventually squashed
c-tso-cactu-misses.notes: Load-unit uops per retired load rise from 11 in Arm mode to 17.96 in TSO mode.

c-tso-outliers.text: On the M4, bwaves, cactuBSSN, wrf and roms run 19 % to 70 % slower in TSO mode on one or four cores
c-tso-outliers.quote: On the M4, the SPEC CPU 2017 programs bwaves, cactuBSSN, wrf, and roms have average slowdowns ranging from 19% to 70% in both single- and multi-core executions

c-tso-overall.text: Leaving out seven outliers, the harmonic-mean TSO-mode slowdown across 49 applications is 1.9 %, most at 3 % or less
c-tso-overall.quote: the harmonic mean [25] of per-application average TSO slowdowns is 1.9%, with most applications exhibiting slowdowns of at most 3%
c-tso-overall.notes: Reported mainly for M4 P cores; the largest non-outlier slowdown is 11.5 %.

c-tso-suite-fixed.text: Across the whole suite the harmonic-mean TSO-mode slowdown is 4.2 %, falling to 1.9 % with allocator and code changes
c-tso-suite-fixed.quote: With these software changes, the harmonic mean of per-application TSO slowdowns across our entire benchmark suite decreases from 4.2% to 1.9%.
c-tso-suite-fixed.notes: Reported mainly for M4 P cores.

c-xnu-a8-loop-buffer.text: Typhoon has a loop buffer, and XNU turns it off (HID0 LoopBuffDisb) to avoid an LSP bug that could wedge the core when CONTEXTIDR is written
c-xnu-a8-loop-buffer.quote: Disable LSP flush with context switch to work around bug in LSP ... that can cause Typhoon to wedge when CONTEXTIDR is written. ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID0_LoopBuffDisb
c-xnu-a8-loop-buffer.notes: Earlier core (A8, Typhoon). Set in the APPLETYPHOON block of start.s at tag xnu-6153.141.1.

c-xnu-a8-l2-starvation.text: Typhoon's L2 has a starvation mode that a snoop evicting an exclusive-monitor line can trigger, and XNU turns that trigger off
c-xnu-a8-l2-starvation.quote: mrs x12, ARM64_REG_HID3 orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID3_DisXmonSnpEvictTriggerL2StarvationMode
c-xnu-a8-l2-starvation.notes: Earlier core (A8). Read from the bit name; Xmon is taken as the exclusive monitor.

c-xnu-a8-hwp-ld-st.text: Typhoon has separate hardware-prefetch disable bits for loads and for stores, and XNU clears both so the prefetchers stay on
c-xnu-a8-hwp-ld-st.quote: and x12, x12, (~ARM64_REG_HID5_DisHwpLd) and x12, x12, (~ARM64_REG_HID5_DisHwpSt)
c-xnu-a8-hwp-ld-st.notes: Earlier core (A8). HWP read as hardware prefetch from the bit names.

c-xnu-a8-dataset-id.text: Core memory requests carry a memcache (SLC) data set ID, and XNU changes its default from 0 to 15 on Typhoon
c-xnu-a8-dataset-id.quote: Change the default memcache data set ID from 0 to 15
c-xnu-a8-dataset-id.notes: Earlier core (A8). The Twister (A9) block sets the same default in four data set ID fields of HID8.

c-xnu-a9-fmul.text: Twister's NEX unit has a fast FP multiply mode, and XNU turns it off for a 4-cycle multiply latency that avoids denormal stalls
c-xnu-a9-fmul.quote: Use 4-cycle MUL latency to avoid denormal stalls ... orr x12, x12, #ARM64_REG_HID7_disNexFastFmul
c-xnu-a9-fmul.notes: Earlier core (A9). The bit name ties NEX to the FP multiplier, which is why NEX is read as the FP/SIMD unit elsewhere.

c-xnu-a10-edb-snoop.text: Hurricane reserves EDB credits for snoops (HID5 CrdEdbSnpRsvd), and XNU raises the reservation to lower the risk of starvation
c-xnu-a10-edb-snoop.quote: Increase Snoop reservation in EDB to reduce starvation risk ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID5_CrdEdbSnpRsvd_VALUE
c-xnu-a10-edb-snoop.notes: Earlier core (A10). EDB is probably the eviction data buffer for dirty L1 victims, a reading of the name.

c-xnu-a10-ic-prefetch.text: Hurricane has an instruction-cache prefetcher with a configurable depth, which XNU sets to 1, and a mode that limits it to one branch
c-xnu-a10-ic-prefetch.quote: IC prefetch configuration ... orr x12, x12, (1 << ARM64_REG_HID0_ICPrefDepth_bshift) orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID0_ICPrefLimitOneBrn
c-xnu-a10-ic-prefetch.notes: Earlier core (A10). What the depth counts (lines or branches) is not stated; read from the field names.

c-xnu-a10-aes-fusion.text: Hurricane can fuse AES pairs that span two decode groups, and XNU turns that cross-group fusion off
c-xnu-a10-aes-fusion.quote: disable crypto fusion across decode groups ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID1_disAESFuseAcrossGrp
c-xnu-a10-aes-fusion.notes: Earlier core (A10). Fusion that crosses a decode-group boundary is the case switched off.

c-xnu-a10x-dczva-cmd.text: On the A10X (Myst) DC ZVA can go out as a command only, without data, and XNU clears the bit that would disable this
c-xnu-a10x-dczva-cmd.quote: Clear DisDcZvaCmdOnly ... Per Myst A0/B0 tunables document ... and x12, x12, ~ARM64_REG_HID3_DisDcZvaCmdOnly
c-xnu-a10x-dczva-cmd.notes: Earlier core (A10X, board T8011). Command-only read from the bit name; a zeroing command without data fits zeroing at the L2.

c-xnu-a11-wkdm-colors.text: On Skye the bus interface returns WKdm write acknowledgements per color, and acknowledgements for both colors can assert together
c-xnu-a11-wkdm-colors.quote: WKdm write ack lost when bif_wke_colorWrAck_XXaH asserts concurrently for both colors
c-xnu-a11-wkdm-colors.notes: Earlier core (A11, all Skye cores). Two colors on write acknowledgements is weak support for color-tagged ordering.

c-xnu-a11-wkdm-strict.text: Skye has a WKdm compression engine (WKE) attached to the bus interface (BIF), and XNU forces it into strict ordering
c-xnu-a11-wkdm-strict.quote: SW WAR/eval: WKdm write ack lost ... orr x12, x12, #ARM64_REG_HID8_WkeForceStrictOrder
c-xnu-a11-wkdm-strict.notes: Earlier core (A11). WKE read as the WKdm engine from the signal name bif_wke.

c-xnu-smb-drain.text: On Skye E-cores a store can be held in an SMB, where it can be invalidated, and the SMB drains by a threshold field that XNU sets to zero
c-xnu-smb-drain.quote: Atomic launch eligibility is erroneously taken away when a store at SMB gets invalidated ... and x12, x12, ~(ARM64_REG_EHID11_SmbDrainThresh_mask)
c-xnu-smb-drain.notes: Earlier core (A11 E-core, Mistral). SMB is read as a store merge buffer; the erratum also shows atomics have a launch eligibility tied to it.

c-xnu-a11-fill-bypass.text: Skye's E-cluster L2 can bypass fill data from either of two pipes straight to an E-core, and XNU turns the bypass off on early silicon
c-xnu-a11-fill-bypass.quote: Disable downstream fill bypass logic ... L2E fill bypass collision from both pipes to ecore
c-xnu-a11-fill-bypass.notes: Earlier core (A11 E-cluster), revisions before B0 only.

c-xnu-a11-nfp-ret-fwd.text: Skye E-cores forward return addresses to the next fetch predictor (NFP), and XNU turns this off on early silicon
c-xnu-a11-nfp-ret-fwd.quote: Disable forwarding of return addresses to the NFP ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_EHID0_nfpRetFwdDisb
c-xnu-a11-nfp-ret-fwd.notes: Earlier core (A11 E-core), revisions before B0 only, after a bug where fetch took an illegal VA exception.

c-xnu-a11-clkdiv-gating.text: Skye cores have clock-divider gating, which XNU turns off on early silicon because of a cluster power-down bug
c-xnu-a11-clkdiv-gating.quote: Disable clock divider gating ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID6_DisClkDivGating
c-xnu-a11-clkdiv-gating.notes: Earlier core (A11), revisions before B0. The name only; how the divider gates the clock is not stated.

c-xnu-a11-acc-link-fsm.text: Powering down a Skye cluster (ACC) runs a link state machine that goes from going-down to cancel, and an upstream drain request can arrive during that switch
c-xnu-a11-acc-link-fsm.quote: ACC power down issue when link FSM switches from GO_DN to CANCEL and at the same time upStreamDrain request is set.
c-xnu-a11-acc-link-fsm.notes: Earlier core (A11). Shows a cluster power-down handshake with the fabric link that can be cancelled.

c-xnu-a11-clock-dither.text: Skye clusters dither their clock, and XNU turns dithering off on early silicon after LLC PIO errors
c-xnu-a11-clock-dither.quote: Disable clock dithering ... [Tunable] Skye A0: Linux: LLC PIO Errors
c-xnu-a11-clock-dither.notes: Earlier core (A11), set in ACC_OVRD and the E-block override. Confirms clock dithering on an earlier core (c-mh-v3-clock-dither).

c-xnu-a12-br-kill-limit.text: Vortex P-cores have a branch kill limit, which XNU enables to stop data corruption from incorrect branch predictor resolution
c-xnu-a12-br-kill-limit.quote: rdar://problem/36716477: data corruption due to incorrect branch predictor resolution ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID1_enaBrKillLimit
c-xnu-a12-br-kill-limit.notes: Earlier core (A12 Vortex), all Aruba parts and Cyprus B0 or later. What the limit counts is not stated.

c-xnu-a12-iex-clock-gating.text: Vortex clock-gates its integer execution (IEX) logic, and XNU forces all IEX level-3 clocks on after segfaults caused by the gating
c-xnu-a12-iex-clock-gating.quote: rdar://problem/34435356: segfaults due to IEX clock-gating ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID1_rccForceAllIexL3ClksOn
c-xnu-a12-iex-clock-gating.notes: Earlier core (A12 P-core). IEX read as the integer execution units.

c-xnu-a12-prefetch-pipe-gating.text: Tempest E-cores clock-gate the prefetcher training pipe with an extended power-saving mode, and XNU reverts it to the default gating
c-xnu-a12-prefetch-pipe-gating.quote: Disable the extension of prefetcher training pipe clock gating, revert to default gating ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_EHID10_rccDisPwrSavePrfClkOff
c-xnu-a12-prefetch-pipe-gating.notes: Earlier core (A12 E-core). The A13 block does the same on its E-cores.

c-xnu-a12-bif-skid.text: The A12X bus interface (BIF) has a fill buffer with a skid buffer behind it, and XNU enables stall logic so the skid buffer cannot overflow
c-xnu-a12-bif-skid.quote: Enable BIF fill buffer stall logic to prevent skid buffer overflow (Aruba A1 only) ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID5_EnableDnFIFORdStall
c-xnu-a12-bif-skid.notes: Earlier chip (A12X Aruba, board T8027), A1 silicon only. The bit names a downstream FIFO read stall.

c-xnu-a12-ordered-ld.text: XNU makes A12 cores hold ordered loads in the LSU until all older loads have completed, because the AF2 fabric's ordering rules allow Arm device-ordering violations
c-xnu-a12-ordered-ld.quote: Prevent ordered loads from being dispatched from LSU until all prior loads have completed. ... AF2 ordering rules allow ARM device ordering violations
c-xnu-a12-ordered-ld.notes: Earlier cores (A12 P and E cores, HID4 ForceNsOrdLdReqNoOlderLd); the A13 block sets it on both core types too. Without the bit, ordered loads leave the LSU earlier and rely on the fabric for order.

c-xnu-a12-poison-barrier.text: On Vortex an older load barrier is meant to redirect a younger load that crosses a poisoned cache line, and it failed to
c-xnu-a12-poison-barrier.quote: [Cyprus Tunable] Poisoned cache line crossing younger load is not redirected by older load-barrier
c-xnu-a12-poison-barrier.notes: Earlier core (A12 P-core). Shows poisoned lines and barrier-driven redirects of younger loads in shipped silicon.

c-xnu-a12-color-opt.text: Vortex and Tempest have a color optimization (HID3 and EHID3 ColorOpt) that XNU turns off to fix the poisoned-load redirect errata
c-xnu-a12-color-opt.quote: Poisoned cache line crossing younger load is not redirected by older load-barrier ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID3_DisColorOpt
c-xnu-a12-color-opt.notes: Earlier cores (A12). The E-core sets EHID3 DisColorOpt for the load-acquire erratum. A color optimization tied to barriers fits color-tagged ordering.

c-xnu-a12-poison-acquire.text: On Tempest E-cores an older load-acquire is meant to redirect a poisoned younger load, and it failed to
c-xnu-a12-poison-acquire.quote: rdar://problem/36595004: Poisoned younger load is not redirected by older load-acquire
c-xnu-a12-poison-acquire.notes: Earlier core (A12 E-core). Load-acquire as well as load barriers redirects poisoned younger loads.

c-xnu-a12-uc-unaligned-store.text: Vortex launches uncacheable unaligned stores early, and XNU turns that off because it broke load-load ordering
c-xnu-a12-uc-unaligned-store.quote: disable faster launches of uncacheable unaligned stores to workaround load/load ordering violation ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID11_DisX64NTLnchOpt
c-xnu-a12-uc-unaligned-store.notes: Earlier core (A12 P-core); the A13 P-core sets the same bit. The bit name points at stores that cross a 64 B line.

c-xnu-a13-stnt-threshold.text: Lightning's LSU has a store non-temporal (STNT) widget that counts contiguous stores, and XNU sets its counter threshold to 3
c-xnu-a13-stnt-threshold.quote: Post-silicon tuning of STNT widget contiguous counter threshold ... orr x12, x12, 3 << ARM64_REG_HID4_CnfCntrThresh_shift
c-xnu-a13-stnt-threshold.notes: Earlier core (A13 Lightning, Cebu B0/B1). XNU also turns the widget off for unaligned stores (HID9 DisSTNTWidgetForUnalign).

c-xnu-a13-stnt-disable.text: Lightning's store non-temporal widget downgrades stores to non-temporal, and XNU turns it off entirely on the P-cores
c-xnu-a13-stnt-disable.quote: rdar://problem/51690962: Disable Store-Non-Temporal downgrade widget ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID4_DisSTNTWidget
c-xnu-a13-stnt-disable.notes: Earlier core (A13 P-core). Set in the same block that tunes the widget's threshold.

c-xnu-a13-x64-barrier.text: On Lightning, loads that cross a 64 B line could break barrier load ordering, fixed by a chicken bit
c-xnu-a13-x64-barrier.quote: Barrier Load Ordering property is not satisfied for x64-loads ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID9_EnableFixBug47221499
c-xnu-a13-x64-barrier.notes: Earlier core (A13 P-core). x64 read as crossing a 64 B boundary, as in the kpep event LDST_X64_UOP.

c-xnu-a13-rf-bank-multipass.text: Lightning's register-file banks can conflict with multipass issue, and the forward-progress widget for that conflict missed livelocks of three or more cycles
c-xnu-a13-rf-bank-multipass.quote: RF bank and Multipass conflict forward progress widget does not handle 3+ cycle livelock
c-xnu-a13-rf-bank-multipass.notes: Earlier core (A13 P-core). Shows a banked register file with read conflicts, not its bank count or power.

c-xnu-a13-xpick-rs45.text: Lightning's reservation stations 4 and 5 can cross-pick work for each other, and RS4 has a secondary mode; XNU enables both to break the livelock
c-xnu-a13-xpick-rs45.quote: orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID16_EnRs4Sec and x12, x12, ~ARM64_REG_HID16_DisxPickRs45 orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID16_EnMPxPick45
c-xnu-a13-xpick-rs45.notes: Earlier core (A13 P-core). Read from the bit names; the same write also sets EnMPCyc7.

c-xnu-a13-nex-pg.text: Lightning P-cores power-gate the NEX unit, and XNU adds 4 dummy pre-cycles because the gating upset temperature-sensor readings
c-xnu-a13-nex-pg.quote: configure dummy cycles to work around incorrect temp sensor readings on NEX power gating ... orr x12, x12, 4 << ARM64_REG_HID13_PreCyc_shift
c-xnu-a13-nex-pg.notes: Earlier core (A13 P-core). NEX read as the FP/SIMD unit (see c-xnu-a9-fmul). Current XNU says NEX power gating is not available on E-cores.

c-xnu-a13-leq-credits.text: Lightning hands out LEQ entries by credits and can throttle them, and XNU makes the throttling aggressive to work around a credit leak
c-xnu-a13-leq-credits.quote: enable aggressive LEQ throttling to work around LEQ credit leak ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID16_leqThrottleAggr
c-xnu-a13-leq-credits.notes: Earlier core (A13 P-core). LEQ read as the load execution queue.

c-xnu-a13-amx-fusion.text: Lightning fuses a direct branch with an AMX (EAS) instruction, which went wrong at a cross-beat location, and the bit XNU sets to stop it is named CacheFusionDisable
c-xnu-a13-amx-fusion.quote: Incorrect fusing of a direct branch with AMX/EAS instruction at cross-beat location ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID0_CacheFusionDisable
c-xnu-a13-amx-fusion.notes: Earlier core (A13 P-core). The bit name hints that fusion is marked in the I-cache, and a beat is probably one fetch read of a line.

c-xnu-a13-sibling-merge.text: The A13 cluster's LLC merges sibling fills, which can let an uncacheable load break Arm ordering, so XNU turns the merge off
c-xnu-a13-sibling-merge.quote: [Cebu ACC Errata] Sibling Merge in LLC can cause UC load to violate ARM Memory Ordering Rules. ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_HID5_DisFill2cMerge
c-xnu-a13-sibling-merge.notes: Earlier chip (A13, all cores). LLC is the cluster L2 in Apple's names; sibling is probably the other 64 B half of a 128 B line, a reading.

c-xnu-a13-uc-stlf.text: Thunder E-cores forward stores to loads even for uncacheable memory, and XNU stops this by forcing such stores to drain first
c-xnu-a13-uc-stlf.quote: Prevent store-to-load forwarding for UC memory to avoid barrier ordering violation ... orr x12, x12, ARM64_REG_EHID10_ForceWStDrainUc
c-xnu-a13-uc-stlf.notes: Earlier core (A13 E-core), only on two-cluster parts.

c-xnu-fs-l1i-256.text: Apple's kernel header gives Firestorm a 256 KB instruction cache
c-xnu-fs-l1i-256.notes: A comment in proc_reg.h. The measured and cache-register value is 192 KiB (c-pac-l1i-size, c-ilk-l1i-size).

c-xnu-fs-l1i-6way.text: Apple's kernel header gives the Firestorm and Icestorm instruction caches 6 ways
c-xnu-fs-l1i-6way.notes: The 6-way follows both sizes, as in the other cores' comments. Agrees with c-pac-l1i-ways and c-ilk-l1i-ways against the inferred 12.

c-xnu-fs-l1d-160.text: Apple's kernel header gives Firestorm a 160 KB data cache
c-xnu-fs-l1d-160.notes: A comment in proc_reg.h. Every measurement gives 128 KiB (l1d.size).

c-xnu-fs-l1d-8way.text: Apple's kernel header gives the Firestorm data cache 8 ways

c-xnu-fs-line-64.text: XNU uses a 64 B line for both the Firestorm instruction and data caches
c-xnu-fs-line-64.quote: I-Cache, 256KB for Firestorm ... #define MMU_I_CLINE 6 /* cache line size as 1<<MMU_I_CLINE (64) */ /* D-Cache, 160KB for Firestorm ... #define MMU_CLINE 6 /* cache line size is 1<<MMU_CLINE (64) */

c-xnu-is-l1i.text: Apple's kernel header gives Icestorm a 128 KB, 6-way instruction cache

c-xnu-is-l1d.text: Apple's kernel header gives Icestorm a 64 KB, 6-way data cache

c-xnu-a13-l1i.text: Apple's kernel header gives Lightning a 192 KB, 6-way instruction cache
c-xnu-a13-l1i.notes: Earlier core (A13). Thunder, its E-core, gets 96 KB.

c-xnu-a13-l1d.text: Apple's kernel header gives Lightning a 128 KB, 8-way data cache

c-xnu-m2-l1i.text: Apple's kernel header gives Avalanche a 192 KB, 6-way instruction cache
c-xnu-m2-l1i.notes: Avalanche is the M2 P-core; Blizzard, its E-core, gets 128 KB.

c-xnu-m2-l1d.text: Apple's kernel header gives Avalanche a 128 KB, 8-way data cache

c-xnu-eret-no-sls.text: On Apple cores an SB or ISB after ERET is technically unnecessary to stop straight-line speculation past the exception return
c-xnu-eret-no-sls.quote: It prevents "straight-line speculation" (an Arm term) past the ERET. ... sb // Technically unnecessary on Apple micro-architectures, may restrict mis-speculation on other architectures
c-xnu-eret-no-sls.notes: Generic code for all Apple cores. Read as the cores not running on past an ERET.

c-xnu-six-nops.text: When SB is unavailable XNU follows ERET with an ISB and six NOPs, which its comment says pad out and terminate the instruction decode group
c-xnu-six-nops.quote: isb // ISB technically unnecessary on Apple micro-architectures, may restrict mis-speculation on other architectures nop // Sequence of six NOPs to pad out and terminate instruction decode group
c-xnu-six-nops.notes: Generic fallback for Apple cores built without SB; cores with SB skip it. The comment does not say which core's decode group the NOPs are sized for.

c-xnu-wfi-power-down.text: Before its final WFI on sleep or shutdown, a core's CPU_OVRD power-down field is set to force-down, so the WFI powers the core off
c-xnu-wfi-power-down.quote: Set "OK to power down" (<rdar://problem/12390433>) mrs x9, CPU_OVRD orr x9, x9, #(ARM64_REG_CYC_OVRD_ok2pwrdn_force_down)
c-xnu-wfi-power-down.notes: Generic code for all Apple cores; builds defining NO_CPU_OVRD skip it.

c-xnu-wfi-clock-gate.text: XNU can force a core's WFI to clock-gate only, keeping the core powered, by setting the same field to force-up
c-xnu-wfi-clock-gate.quote: Force WFI to use clock gating only ... orr x0, x0, #(ARM64_REG_CYC_OVRD_ok2pwrdn_force_up)
c-xnu-wfi-clock-gate.notes: Generic code for all Apple cores; on other Arm cores the same routine does nothing.

c-xnu-acc-deep-sleep.text: Cluster deep sleep is set up in ACC_OVRD, whose fields for the L2 flush on cluster sleep, SRM power-down, link train-down and CPM power-down each take a deep-sleep value
c-xnu-acc-deep-sleep.quote: Enable deep sleep mrs x1, ACC_OVRD orr x1, x1, #(ARM64_REG_ACC_OVRD_enDeepSleep) ... ARM64_REG_ACC_OVRD_disL2Flush4AccSlp_deepsleep) ... ARM64_REG_ACC_OVRD_ok2PwrDnSRM_deepsleep) ... ARM64_REG_ACC_OVRD_ok2TrDnLnk_deepsleep) ... ARM64_REG_ACC_OVRD_ok2PwrDnCPM_deepsleep)
c-xnu-acc-deep-sleep.notes: The fields are defined for every Apple core after A9; this path runs on builds with the global sleep bit. On A11 the E and P blocks each have their own copy.

c-xnu-irq-mask-wfi.text: On multi-cluster chips XNU masks IRQ and FIQ at the core through CPU_OVRD before a power-down WFI, so they cannot wake it spuriously
c-xnu-irq-mask-wfi.quote: Mask FIQ and IRQ to avoid spurious wakeups ... mov x10, #(ARM64_REG_CYC_OVRD_irq_disable | ARM64_REG_CYC_OVRD_fiq_disable)
c-xnu-irq-mask-wfi.notes: Built for multi-cluster (HAS_CLUSTER) parts such as the M1, and only outside deep sleep; builds with NO_CPU_OVRD mask the timer interrupt instead.

c-xnu-bp-retention.text: XNU has a routine that lets branch predictor state be kept across cluster (ACC) sleep, chosen by a boot argument
c-xnu-bp-retention.quote: Helper function to enable branch predictor state retention ... across ACC sleep
c-xnu-bp-retention.notes: Built only with HAS_BP_RET, which the A13-era start.s already calls, so some core up to the A13 has it; the cores are not named. The register header names two sleep-enable bits, bdpSlpEn and btpSlpEn.

c-xnu-core-throttle-rate.text: Each Apple core has a memory-mapped throttle register, CORE_THRTL_CFG2, with an 8-bit throttle-rate field named c1pptThrtlRate
c-xnu-core-throttle-rate.notes: Defined for all Apple cores without a condition; the code read here does not show how it is set.

c-xnu-fast-ipi-types.text: A fast IPI request names one of four types, immediate, retract, deferred or no-wake
c-xnu-fast-ipi-types.notes: Built only with HAS_IPI. XNU's IPI code cites the Skye (A11) ACC spec; current XNU uses the same code on every core built with HAS_IPI.

c-xnu-ipi-deferred-timer.text: A deferred fast IPI waits for a countdown kept in REFCLK ticks in a 16-bit field of a global register, and XNU's default is 64 µs
c-xnu-ipi-deferred-timer.quote: #define kDeferredIPITimerDefault (64 * NSEC_PER_USEC) ... adjust IPI_CR timer countdown value for deferred IPI ... clamp maximum REFCLK ticks to 0xFFFF (16 bit field) ... from Skye ACC user spec section 5.7.3.3
c-xnu-ipi-deferred-timer.notes: The 64 µs is a kernel default that a boot argument can change. The register layout comes from the Skye (A11) ACC spec.

c-xnu-ipicr-two-copies.text: On Skye the IPI control register has one copy in the P block and one in the E block, and a system-register write travels as a token around both CPM rings to update both
c-xnu-ipicr-two-copies.quote: IPICR is a global register but there are two copies in ACC: one at pBLK and one at eBLK. ... IPICR write SPR token also traverses both pCPM and eCPM rings and updates both copies.
c-xnu-ipicr-two-copies.notes: Earlier chip (A11), whose P and E cores share one ACC.

c-xnu-dcache-fully-coherent.text: On Apple cores, cleaning the data cache to the point of unification is an empty routine, because the caches are fully coherent
c-xnu-dcache-fully-coherent.notes: Generic code for all Apple cores; clean and flush to the point of coherency are empty too. Contradicts the mechanism in part, since new code needs no data-side clean before the I-cache invalidate.

c-xnu-icache-invalidate.text: To make new code visible XNU still invalidates the instruction cache, line by line with IC IVAU when the I-cache does not alias, otherwise in full
c-xnu-icache-invalidate.quote: bl EXT(CleanPoU_DcacheRegion) #if __ARM_IC_NOALIAS_ICACHE__ ... ic ivau, x0 // Invalidate icache line ... #else bl EXT(InvalidatePoU_Icache)
c-xnu-icache-invalidate.notes: Generic code for all Apple cores; the full invalidate is IC IALLUIS. Which cores build with the non-aliasing flag is not stated.

c-xnu-dc-cvac-nop.text: DC CVAC does nothing on Apple cores, so XNU cleans to the point of coherency with DC CIVAC, clean and invalidate
c-xnu-dc-cvac-nop.quote: It may be tempting to clean the cache (dc cvac), but it's always a NOP on ... Apple hardware. dc civac, x0
c-xnu-dc-cvac-nop.notes: Generic code for all Apple cores. The older tag says the same of Cyclone only.

c-xnu-dc-mva-toggle.text: Apple cores have a HID4 bit (EHID4 on E-cores) that turns off data-cache maintenance by VA, and XNU's cache code can toggle it
c-xnu-dc-mva-toggle.quote: Disables cache maintenance by VA instructions on Apple SoCs.
c-xnu-dc-mva-toggle.notes: At the A13-era tag, boot code common to all Apple cores sets this bit, and a second one for set/way operations on the L2 (DisDcSWL2Ops).

c-zhou-ibtb.text: Firestorm's indirect BTB holds 1024 entries and Icestorm's 512; it is a tagged cache, not indexed by branch address
c-zhou-ibtb.quote: which means the size of iBTB is 512 entries on icestorm, 1024 entries on firestorm
