l1i_tree_plru.name: Tree-PLRU L1I replacement
l1i_tree_plru.description: The L1I picks its victim by tree pseudo-LRU over its six ways, as three pairs, like the L1D.
l1i_tree_plru.detection_rule: An eviction sequence built on tree-PLRU state evicts the predicted code line, as Prime+Retouch showed for the L1D.

l1i_maintenance_only.name: Code changes by cache maintenance only
l1i_maintenance_only.description: The L1I does not snoop stores; code written at run time is cleaned to the L2 and invalidated by line, and the L2 forwards the invalidate through its copies of the L1 tags.
l1i_maintenance_only.alternative: The L1I snoops stores to lines it holds and drops them itself.
l1i_maintenance_only.detection_rule: Code rewritten without an I-cache invalidate keeps running its old instructions.

path_history_rewind.name: Path history rewind
path_history_rewind.description: Each branch in flight records the head of a circular buffer of taken-branch footprints; a mispredict rewinds the head to that mark and pushes the corrected outcome.
path_history_rewind.alternative: Each branch saves full copies of both history registers, restored on a mispredict.
path_history_rewind.detection_rule: No timing probe tells them apart; the simulator can carry either.

l1d_write_allocate.name: Write-allocate L1D with store-miss entries
l1d_write_allocate.description: A store miss takes a store-miss entry that fetches the line for ownership while younger store hits write ahead of it; full-line streaming stores skip the fetch and go out non-temporal.
l1d_write_allocate.alternative: Stores that miss write around the L1D into the L2.
l1d_write_allocate.detection_rule: A load right after a store that missed hits the L1D if the store allocated the line, and goes to the L2 if it wrote around.

fill_buffer_pool.name: Shared fill buffers with line merging
fill_buffer_pool.description: One fill buffer per 64 B line in flight, shared by demand loads and L1 prefetches; a second miss to the line joins its entry, and a load that finds the buffers full replays.
fill_buffer_pool.alternative: Each miss holds its own entry, and a second miss to a line waits until the first fills.
fill_buffer_pool.detection_rule: Independent loads to distinct lines level off at the buffer count, while loads to one line keep scaling past it.

l2_core_round_robin.name: Round-robin among cores at the L2
l2_core_round_robin.description: Per-core request queues feed each L2 bank round-robin, demand ahead of prefetch, cores in latency mode first.
l2_core_round_robin.alternative: Requests from all cores enter one queue in arrival order.
l2_core_round_robin.detection_rule: With three cores streaming through the L2, a fourth core's pointer chase keeps its unloaded latency under round-robin and slows with the load under one shared queue.

address_interleave_hash.name: Hashed address interleave
address_interleave_hash.description: Addresses are hashed across the coherence, SLC and memory-controller pipelines and over DRAM channels, ranks and banks; later patents let the OS shut an idle controller after moving its pages.

noc_layout.name: Layered fabric, one port per cluster
noc_layout.description: Each CPU cluster is one requester on a coherent fabric joining memory, SLC, CPU and GPU through switch levels, bridged to a non-coherent IO fabric for PCIe and USB.

noc_rings_lanes.name: Later NoCs: rings, lanes, split networks
noc_rings_lanes.description: Later NoCs use two counter-rotating rings, add a parallel lane for bandwidth, split CPU, IO and GPU networks, and give each P-cluster two ports chosen by address hash.

noc_split_paths.name: Separate command and data paths
noc_split_paths.description: Commands and data travel apart: write data is buffered once at fabric entry and moved once, only a small control packet is routed, and most read returns skip Coherence.

remote_maintenance_pacing.name: Paced remote maintenance
remote_maintenance_pacing.description: Cache and TLB maintenance requests wait in a per-cluster unit, and a core that has taken many refuses more until it progresses; a later design poisons invalidated lines and syncs them later.

same_address_ordering.name: Linked same-address waiting
same_address_ordering.description: A request blocked by same-address work waits linked behind it in a retry queue, a pending SLC line or a hashed write table, or retries once the blocking transaction's response passes.

slc_io_cache_proxy.name: SLC as controller for IO caches
slc_io_cache_proxy.description: The SLC acts as cache controller for small caches in IO blocks outside the coherence domain, turning one request into the simpler commands such a cache needs.

unshared_snoop_skip.name: Snoop skipping for unshared lines
unshared_snoop_skip.description: Lines in pages marked never-shared, or lines a device has learned no other requester can hold, skip snoop broadcasts.

amx_datapath.name: AMX outer-product grid
amx_datapath.description: AMX accumulates X-by-Y outer products into Z, held across an 8x8 grid of processing elements, and runs a load or store to the L2 alongside each arithmetic operation.

amx_lsu_issue.name: AMX issue through the store queue
amx_lsu_issue.description: AMX instructions pass through the core's load/store pipeline, wait in the store queue until non- speculative, and go to AMX over the L2 bus, up to two a cycle, in bundles of three or four.

amx_op_set.name: AMX operation set
amx_op_set.description: AMX multiply-adds and -subtracts outer products in fp64, fp32, fp16 and int16, with no int8; patents add 2x2 packing, lookup tables, strided dots, mixed precision and row moves.

amx_shared_contexts.name: One AMX unit per cluster
amx_shared_contexts.description: One AMX unit per P-cluster serves its cores, keeping a full register set for each, and a queue monitor tells the OS when several cores overload it.

clock_ramp.name: Clock ramp from idle
clock_ramp.description: From idle the P-cluster clock starts rising within about 10 to 20 ms and reaches its maximum after roughly 40 to 100 ms, in steps that may be set by hardware.

core_power_cycle.name: Core power-down and restart
core_power_cycle.description: A powered-down core restarts from an address the always-on power manager supplies and reloads its saved state from the L2, the SLC or DRAM, depending on what else slept.

dvfs_transition.name: DVFS transition sequence
dvfs_transition.description: A cluster's cores, L2 and bus interface change performance state together: voltage rises and is sensed settled first, then the PLL retargets behind a divider stepping from 4 to 1.

interrupt_routing.name: Power-aware interrupt routing
interrupt_routing.description: Device interrupts follow the device's writes, are held while all cores sleep, and are offered cluster by cluster in soft, hard and force rounds that a busy core may refuse.

perf_controller.name: Closed-loop performance controller
perf_controller.description: A closed-loop controller maps each thread group's control effort to a cluster type and DVFS level, and raises NoC, DRAM or feeding-cluster clocks when cores stall on memory.

predictive_clock_crossing.name: Predictive clock-domain crossing
predictive_clock_crossing.description: Clock-domain crossings predict the other clock's edges from history instead of using two-cycle synchronizers, passing one-bit pointer increments through small event FIFOs.

slc_address_ranges.name: Address ranges held in the SLC
slc_address_ranges.description: Range registers can map an address range into SLC lines as memory, such as camera or static display frames, or let a filtered range keep only part of its lines.

slc_line_states.name: SLC line states and sectors
slc_line_states.description: SLC lines hold only invalid, valid and modified states with per-sector valid flags; partial writes keep a byte mask, and later designs track dirtiness per 64 B half.

slc_memory_side.name: Memory-side SLC
slc_memory_side.description: The SLC sits behind coherence as a front end owned by the memory controller, caching any range, even uncacheable ones, and a write that reaches it counts as written to DRAM.

slc_slices.name: SLC slices
slc_slices.description: The SLC is split into slices picked by physical address bits or a hash, each behind its own arbiter; readings give two slices (even and odd lines) or four on the M1.

cluster_compression_engines.name: Cluster page-compression engines
cluster_compression_engines.description: Each cluster has WKDM and LZ page-compression engines at the L2, fed through a core's store pipeline like AMX, which the OS uses under a backlog or to save power or heat.

dram_clock_scaling.name: DRAM frequency scaling
dram_clock_scaling.description: DRAM latency varies widely and drops under heavier DRAM load, which is put down to the DRAM clock rising with demand.

dram_power_states.name: DRAM power states
dram_power_states.description: When quiet, the memory controller and DRAM drop to half clock or self-refresh with writes held; DRAM performance states are revisited every 50 µs to 20 ms and the PHY recalibrates at run time.

dram_qos_scheduler.name: DRAM bank scheduler
dram_qos_scheduler.description: Each DRAM bank picks its highest-category request from per-page and per-channel lists, favouring page hits up to a streak cap; waiting requests gain priority with age or merging.

dram_refresh_scheduling.name: Flexible refresh placement
dram_refresh_scheduling.description: Bank refreshes slip within a refresh window, first into write turns, then into read turns, and are forced with a shorter window and lookahead once time runs short.

dram_rw_turns.name: Read and write turns
dram_rw_turns.description: The controller leaves write mode by write-queue watermarks, earlier when latency tolerance is low or low-latency reads wait, and sizes turns against an access-efficiency target.

mc_write_merge.name: Write merging in the memory controller
mc_write_merge.description: Writes to one address merge by byte enable; a read overlapping a queued partial write goes first and takes the write data on its way out, and read-modify-write reads end a read turn.

pattern_index_transfer.name: Data-pattern transfer compression
pattern_index_transfer.description: Caches track common data patterns, such as all zeros, and send a pattern index over the NoC instead of the data.

shared_rw_memory_path.name: Shared load/store path beyond the L2
shared_rw_memory_path.description: Loads and stores share one path through DRAM and probably the NoC and SLC, so mixing them adds no bandwidth and costs none; DRAM read-write turnaround stays hidden.

ecores_share_pl2.name: E cores use the P-cluster L2
ecores_share_pl2.description: While the P cores sleep the E cores can use the P cluster's L2, which then stays powered and takes its DVFS state from the E cores.

l2_core_lru.name: Per-core LRU in the L2
l2_core_lru.description: L2 replacement follows LRU order among lines from one core but not when lines from different cores share a set, so a cross-core eviction set needs several passes.

l2_half_lines.name: Two L1 lines per L2 line
l2_half_lines.description: Each 128 B L2 line holds two 64 B L1 lines that fill and evict on their own; one study finds only the accessed half enters the L1, another finds both halves do.

l2_hashed_way_filter.name: Hashed L2 index with partial-tag way filter
l2_hashed_way_filter.description: The L2 index seems hashed, so some strides crowd onto a fraction of the cache, and an early partial-tag compare limits which ways are read instead of a full tag compare per way.

l2_line_ordering.name: Per-line ordering at the L2
l2_line_ordering.description: Requests queued at the L2 stay in order within one 128 B L2 line but not across lines, so a core's read may pass its own write to the other half of a line.

l2_physical_index.name: Physical L2 index
l2_physical_index.description: The L2 picks one of 8192 sets from physical address bits in the page offset and page frame; one study finds two of the bits are XORs of higher page-number bits.

l2_zero_line_tags.name: Zero-line tags and loser bank
l2_zero_line_tags.description: All-zero lines are recorded as a tag bit without touching the data array, and invalid and zero lines share a loser bank kept powered off until real data needs it.

uncached_line_handling.name: Uncacheable line handling
uncached_line_handling.description: Uncacheable reads fill a few L2 ways set aside for them or merge in per-controller buffers, and uncacheable writes are gathered into full lines that skip the L1 and L2.

agu_same_page_check.name: Early same-page address check
agu_same_page_check.description: During address generation a masked compare tells whether base plus offset stays on the base register's page without waiting for the full add.

ldpq_lsu_split.name: Vector load pair split at cache access
ldpq_lsu_split.description: An LDP of Q registers is one instruction through rename and the ROB and splits into two 16 B cache requests only at cache access; an LDP of X registers stays one request.

lsu_load_to_load_bypass.name: Load-to-load address bypass in the LSU
lsu_load_to_load_bypass.description: A load whose base comes from a just-issued load that hit the L1 takes the value inside the LSU, 3 cycles instead of 4; for an LDP only the first register qualifies.

redundant_mem_op_elim.name: Removal of repeated loads and stores
redundant_mem_op_elim.description: Back-to-back identical loads or identical stores all execute; none is removed as redundant.

spec_fault_no_access.name: No speculative access to faulting addresses
spec_fault_no_access.description: A speculative load or fetch through a pointer that failed its AUT check is not performed and leaves no TLB trace, and no Meltdown-style reads across address spaces are seen.

split_access_handling.name: Line- and page-crossing accesses
split_access_handling.description: An unaligned or line-crossing access stays one op that sends two line requests for about one cycle more; a page-crossing load takes about 28 to 31 cycles more, presumed microcode.

sq_partial_forwarding.name: Partial store-to-load forwarding
sq_partial_forwarding.description: A load overlapping queued stores takes their bytes and the rest from the L1 at full rate; combining bytes from two store-queue entries costs about one extra cycle.

store_load_dep_predictor.name: Store/load PC-pair dependence predictor
store_load_dep_predictor.description: A table of about 74 store/load PC pairs makes a matching load wait for its store; other loads are predicted not to alias, and entries are replaced round-robin.

stxr_barrier_fusion.name: Store-exclusive and barrier fusion
stxr_barrier_fusion.description: A store-exclusive and the barrier right after it fuse in the LSU into one operation that needs a single trip to the point of coherency.

cold_start_mode.name: Cold-start fetch and predictor mode
cold_start_mode.description: After power-up with empty caches, each instruction miss to the L2 brings three lines, and a new branch is written into four TAGE entries instead of one or two.

l1i_predecode.name: I-cache predecode on fill
l1i_predecode.description: Lines are predecoded on fill: calls and returns are marked, PC-relative branch targets keep their low 14 bits, and all undefined encodings become one value.

l1i_way_prediction.name: I-cache way and translation from predictors
l1i_way_prediction.description: The fetch predictor and a sequential way predictor supply the I-cache way and translation, so most fetches read one way and skip the iTLB and tag lookups.

nfp_training.name: Fetch-predictor training and hysteresis
nfp_training.description: The slower predictors that check the fetch predictor also write it; hysteresis keeps an entry until it is wrong twice, and a new entry meeting a strong set goes to a FIFO overflow table.

predictor_power_gating.name: Predictor power gating
predictor_power_gating.description: Fetch-predictor entries record which predictors the coming groups need so the others are clock-gated, and TAGE tables are probed in stages or powered off when little used.

retire_time_training.name: Branch information tables and retire-time training
retire_time_training.description: Each branch carries its predictor indices and state from decode to retire in branch information tables; predictors train at retire, only on mispredictions or weak predictions.

loop_predictor.name: Companion loop predictor
loop_predictor.description: A small loop predictor beside TAGE takes over in loops so the TAGE tables can be shut down soon after loop mode starts.

tage_tables.name: TAGE table layout
tage_tables.description: Six tagged tables, each with its own associativity, are indexed by PC bits 18:2 and history and split by PC bit 6, so two branches in one block are read together.

ras_overflow_clear.name: Return stack cleared on overflow
ras_overflow_clear.description: Once calls nest deeper than the return stack, call and return time rises sharply, read as the core clearing the stack on overflow.

ras_pac_check.name: Pointer authentication at the RAS
ras_pac_check.description: Pointer authentication codes in the high bits of return addresses are checked in the logic that pushes and pops the return stack.

return_fetch_table.name: Return fetch table
return_fetch_table.description: Fetch groups ending in a return sit in a separate table holding no target or length; the RAS gives the target, and fetch after the return assumes the maximum length.

two_level_ras.name: Decode RAS with fetch mini-RAS
two_level_ras.description: The main return stack is kept at decode, and a small fetch-side stack covers only returns whose calls decode has not yet seen.

judgment.text: Both patents predate the M1, and nothing measured goes against a main stack at decode with a small fetch-side stack.

ittage_indirect.name: Tagged history tables for indirect targets
ittage_indirect.description: Indirect targets come from tagged tables indexed by PC and path history, with usefulness bits and hysteresis that keeps a target until it misses twice.

objc_msgsend_predictor.name: objc_msgSend method predictor
objc_msgsend_predictor.description: For one configured hot indirect branch, a predict uop hashes the class and selector registers into a method cache that redirects fetch; the M1 lacks it.

next_fetch_groups.name: Next-fetch-predictor fetch groups
next_fetch_groups.description: The fetch predictor, indexed and tagged by the fetch PC, gives the next fetch group's target, length and ending branch type; one group, ending at a taken branch, is fetched per cycle.

staged_fetch_redirect.name: Staged fetch redirects
staged_fetch_redirect.description: Slower predictors and decode check the single-cycle fetch prediction and refetch in a few cycles when they disagree, well short of a flush; fetch halts when no target is known.

wrong_path_redirect.name: Wrong-path branch redirect
wrong_path_redirect.description: A mispredicted indirect branch on the wrong path of an older mispredict is squashed as soon as its target is computed, and fetch moves to that target.

load_op_fusion.name: Load-op fusion
load_op_fusion.description: A small ALU in the load/store unit applies an ADD, XOR, shift, rotate, CBZ or TBZ decoded in the same cycle to the loaded value; the M1 has no load-op fusion.

speculation_barriers.name: Barriers that stop speculation
speculation_barriers.description: A CSDB or ISB placed after a bounds check stops speculative execution past a mispredicted branch; a DMB or DSB on its own does not.

uop_split_merge.name: Uop splitting and merging
uop_split_merge.description: Shifted or extended ALU ops are one uop that issues twice, LDP and fused pairs issue once, NOP and B never issue, and pre- or post-indexed accesses add a base-update uop.

judgment.text: NOPs never issue and use no unit, but they are not dropped at decode; each takes a retire slot, which is why over 2200 fit in the window.

iq_bypass_fixup.name: Instruction-queue bypass and fix-up
iq_bypass_fixup.description: Fetch bypasses the instruction queue when it is empty; in the queue, instructions a taken short forward branch skips are deleted without resteering fetch.

judgment.text: Likely for bypassing an empty queue. Deleting the instructions a short forward branch skips comes from a post-M1 patent and stays open.

control_independence.name: Reuse past reconvergence
control_independence.description: After a mispredicted short forward branch, loads past the reconvergence point that do not depend on the wrong path keep their values, and branch outcomes there pass to fetch.

group_map.name: Group dependency map
group_map.description: A Map stage ahead of Rename resolves register dependences among the up to eight instructions of a cycle, so chains of eliminated scalar moves still complete at rename.

macro_op_fusion.name: Macro-op fusion
macro_op_fusion.description: Decode spots pairs (an ALU op and a following conditional branch, cbz or cbnz; AES and PMULL pairs; AMX pairs) and Map merges them into one uop; adrp+add and mov+movk do not fuse.

move_elimination.name: Move elimination and zeroing
move_elimination.description: Full-width register moves finish at rename and vector zeroing costs nothing; sub-register moves, MOV from xzr and EOR self-zeroing run as ordinary ops.

speculative_special_regs.name: Speculative special-register writes
speculative_special_regs.description: Flag moves are handled at the rename map, and other special-register writes go out of order into speculative storage made permanent at retire, so they do not serialize.

writeback_overflow_pool.name: Writeback overflow pool
writeback_overflow_pool.description: Results beyond the register file's write ports go to a temporary pool and drain later instead of stalling issue.

split_flag_files.name: Split flag register files
split_flag_files.description: Scalar and SIMD/fp code keep separate condition-flag register files; flag chains within a domain cost nothing, and moving flags across costs about six cycles.

issue_age_flush.name: Age bits for mispredict flush
issue_age_flush.description: One possibly-mispredicting op issues per cycle, and age bits built from short per-entry offsets tell recovery which younger work in each pipeline to flush.

matrix_scheduler.name: Matrix scheduler
matrix_scheduler.description: Queues do not shift: a dependency matrix indexed by scheduler entry wakes dependents over a wide bus, an age matrix picks the oldest ready uop, and operands are read at issue.

judgment.text: Nothing measured goes against it, and it fits operands read at issue from queues that do not shift.

load_replay_shadow.name: Load replay with a shadow window
load_replay_shadow.description: Uops issued behind a load stay in their queue under a shadow timer and reissue if the load replays; the replaying load waits in a load execution queue bank of its pipe.

divider_pipe.name: Side-pipeline integer divider
divider_pipe.description: The integer divider is a separate pipeline behind one unit's queue: back-to-back divides issue every other cycle, and other work on that unit is not held up.

exec_forwarding.name: Forwarding and domain crossing
exec_forwarding.description: Integer-to-SIMD moves and conversions travel through a load slot as a fake load and the reverse use a dedicated path, about six cycles each way; a MADD feeds the next addend in one cycle.

fp_back_to_back_fusion.name: Back-to-back FADD fusion
fp_back_to_back_fusion.description: A dependent pair of FADDs is fused back to back, taking 5 cycles instead of 6.

abandonable_requests.name: Abandonable cache requests
abandonable_requests.description: Prefetches, instruction fetches and speculative loads are flagged abandonable, so on an interrupt the caches may drop them and the core drains faster.

late_ordering_check.name: Late store/load address recheck
late_ordering_check.description: The store/load address check is repeated as the load's data reaches its register, so a store address resolving two to four cycles late causes a replay, not a flush.

sq_32b_slots.name: 32 B store-queue slots over 16 B store paths
sq_32b_slots.description: Store-queue slots seem to be 32 B and gather stores within a slot, a line-crossing store taking two; stores reach the L1D over 16 B paths with no full-line write.

cache_subarray_power.name: SRAM sub-array power-down
cache_subarray_power.description: Caches are built from many small SRAM sub-arrays on a separate supply that power down when idle and precharge on demand; waking may reject an L1D load for a cycle.

fill_bank_conflicts.name: L1D fills take bank cycles from loads
fill_bank_conflicts.description: Lines prefetched from the L2 wait in buffers and are written into the L1D banks, blocking loads to those banks and costing about one cycle in seven; stores see no such loss.

l1_l2_coherence_limit.name: L1-L2 coherence work limits mixed traffic
l1_l2_coherence_limit.description: Coherence work between the L1 and the L2, perhaps one line every other cycle, caps L1 copies near 150 GB/s and mixed load/store traffic in the L2 near 100 GB/s.

l1d_page_offset_index.name: Page-offset L1D index
l1d_page_offset_index.description: The L1D set comes from address bits 6-13, inside the 16 KiB page offset, so the cache is indexed by the virtual address.

l1d_tree_plru.name: Tree-PLRU L1D replacement
l1d_tree_plru.description: Each 8-way L1D set picks its victim by a tree pseudo-LRU, and access sequences built on that state produce the predicted misses.

cluster_l2_tlb.name: Cluster-shared L2 TLB
cluster_l2_tlb.description: Cores keep small L1 TLBs, while the L2 TLB and the page walkers sit beside the L2 in a unit the cluster's cores share.

dtlb_random_replacement.name: Random L1 dTLB replacement
dtlb_random_replacement.description: The L1 dTLB seems to replace entries at random, since latency past its capacity climbs linearly from 3 to 9 cycles instead of stepping.

indexed_page_permissions.name: Indexed page permissions
indexed_page_permissions.description: A page holds an index into a 4-entry permission table instead of permission bits, so one core can switch a page's permissions without a TLB shootdown.

mmu_walk_cache.name: Page walks through an MMU walk cache
mmu_walk_cache.description: L2 TLB misses walk a three-level 16 KiB page table through an MMU walk cache for the upper levels, with leaf entries read from the L2.

tlb_invalidation_shortcuts.name: Faster TLB invalidation
tlb_invalidation_shortcuts.description: A range invalidation picks the faster of scanning all entries or looking up each page, ASID/VMID fields are striped to compare four at once, and accelerator invalidations are bundled.

tlb_mixed_page_sizes.name: Mixed page sizes in one TLB
tlb_mixed_page_sizes.description: TLB entries carry a page-size field so one TLB holds up to five sizes, and a per-context presence vector limits lookups to sizes in use; the M1 shows only 16 KiB pages.

ampm_prefetcher.name: Access-map prefetcher with stride side tables
ampm_prefetcher.description: An access-map prefetcher matches region line maps against stride and density patterns, helped by large- stride and SMS tables; the M1 shows stride, region and hybrid prefetching.

prefetch_throttle.name: Prefetch throttling
prefetch_throttle.description: Every 32 cycles the L2 rates its per-core prefetch queues and sets a throttle level; credits cap a region at about four prefetches in flight, and prefetch grows bolder when misses return late.

temporal_prefetch.name: Temporal history prefetcher
temporal_prefetch.description: A temporal prefetcher with a GHB-like history of a little under 256 entries covers random accesses inside a 15 KiB region but not inside a 16 KiB one.

retire_groups.name: Coalesced retire groups
retire_groups.description: Uops retire in groups of up to seven; a memory op starts a group and a branch ends one.
retire_groups.detection_rule: NOP knee divided by load, store or branch knee is close to a whole number >= 2

rename_retire_queue.name: Rename retire queue (history file)
rename_retire_queue.description: A second queue of about 620 entries limits instructions that change the register map.
rename_retire_queue.detection_rule: register-writing fillers knee far below the NOP knee and above the physical register count

lsq_at_issue.name: Load/store queue entries allocated at issue
lsq_at_issue.description: Load and store queue entries are taken at issue, not at dispatch.
lsq_at_issue.detection_rule: same filler gives different knees under a miss delay and an ALU delay

judgment.text: Allocation at issue explains why the apparent queue sizes change with the delay used (about 330, 125 and 100, 188 and 118).

register_security_tag.name: Register mapping security tag
register_security_tag.description: Reading a register the process has not written slows integer issue to about 4-wide.
register_security_tag.detection_rule: throughput drop when reading unclaimed registers

decoupled_fetch.name: Decoupled fetch with fetch-directed prefetch
decoupled_fetch.description: Fetch is not fully decoupled from branch prediction on the M1.
decoupled_fetch.detection_rule: I-cache miss cost drops under predictable branches for footprints larger than L1I

streaming_store_nt.name: Automatic non-temporal streaming stores
streaming_store_nt.description: Streaming stores become non-temporal without software hints.
streaming_store_nt.detection_rule: full-line streaming stores show no read-for-ownership traffic, so streaming write bandwidth beats partial-line writes

one_core_dram_saturation.name: One core saturates DRAM
one_core_dram_saturation.description: A single Firestorm core draws nearly all of the M1's DRAM bandwidth, so more cores add none and congestion lowers the total.
one_core_dram_saturation.detection_rule: Aggregate DRAM read bandwidth with two to four cores streaming is no higher than with one core, and may be lower.

banked_lsq.name: Two-bank load and store queues
banked_lsq.description: The load queue interleaves its entries over two banks, and the store queue fills one bank with a contiguous run of stores while the other drains in order; each bank retires one entry a cycle under pointers the banks exchange.
banked_lsq.detection_rule: Draining the load or store queue would top out at one entry per bank per cycle, two in all, however many entries are ready to leave.

hierarchical_reservation_station.name: Two-level reservation station
hierarchical_reservation_station.description: A scheduler queue holds its highest-priority ops in a primary buffer and the rest in a secondary buffer, each picked by its own logic; secondary picks fill issue slots the primary leaves empty, and the oldest secondary ops move up as room frees.
hierarchical_reservation_station.detection_rule: With the front of a queue full of stalled old ops, a young independent op further back would still issue, but perhaps a cycle later than an op near the front.

lsq_early_release.name: Early release of load/store queue entries
lsq_early_release.description: Loads and non-speculative stores give back their queue entries before retiring.
lsq_early_release.detection_rule: the same load or store filler gives a larger knee with no older store pending than with one

l1i_vipt.name: Virtually indexed, physically tagged L1I
l1i_vipt.description: The L1I takes its set index from the virtual address and checks a physical tag, on both core types.
l1i_vipt.detection_rule: Code reached through two virtual mappings of one page that differ in index bits above the page offset occupies two L1I sets.

path_history_shift_xor.name: Path history register (shift-and-XOR)
path_history_shift_xor.description: The 100-bit history shifts and XORs in branch address bits, not outcomes.
path_history_shift_xor.detection_rule: two paths that differ in one bit of one earlier branch's PC or target give a spy branch with opposite outcomes ~0 % mispredicts while the bit is in the history and ~25 % (3-bit counters) once it has aged out

bpu_isolation.name: Branch predictor context isolation
bpu_isolation.description: The conditional predictor keeps no privilege or process tag.
bpu_isolation.detection_rule: out-of-place mistraining of a victim branch from another privilege level or process, with matching low-32-bit addresses and history, gives the victim ~25 % mispredicts when entries are shared and ~0 % when they are isolated

l1i_coupled_btb.name: Branch targets tied to the L1I
l1i_coupled_btb.description: A branch that misses the first-level BTB takes its target from the L1I, with a two-cycle bubble.
l1i_coupled_btb.detection_rule: taken-branch latency steps with code footprint (branch spacing) more than with branch count

amx_z_dependency_window.name: AMX out-of-order window without Z renaming
amx_z_dependency_window.description: AMX reorders operations within a small buffer but does not rename Z, so an operation into a Z range waits out the 4-cycle FMA latency of the last one there, and a core needs four independent Z ranges to issue an outer product every cycle.
amx_z_dependency_window.detection_rule: One core's outer-product throughput rises in step with the number of independent Z accumulators up to four and then stays flat, while a second core's own Z adds more.

load_value_prediction.name: Load value prediction
load_value_prediction.description: A PC-tagged predictor hands a load's last constant value to dependent instructions early; not found on M1 or M2, present from M3/A17 Pro.
load_value_prediction.detection_rule: a chain of dependent byte loads from shuffled, cache-missing lines runs at the same speed whether every line holds one constant or random values; with the predictor the constant run speeds up after about 40 loads

ibp_context_check.name: Indirect target context check
ibp_context_check.description: Indirect-predictor entries are shared across privilege levels and ASIDs; a target trained in another context is fetched but not executed.
ibp_context_check.detection_rule: train an indirect branch in one context and run an identically placed copy at another EL or ASID; the trained target's I-cache line comes back fetched (Flush+Reload hit) while a load at the target stays at SLC latency

phantom_fetch.name: Phantom fetch on non-branches
phantom_fetch.description: A non-branch at the address of a trained branch redirects fetch to the trained target, which is fetched but never executed.
phantom_fetch.detection_rule: train a branch, replace it with a NOP at the same address and run it; the old target's I-cache line comes back fetched while a load at the target stays at SLC latency

zero_cycle_loads.name: Zero-cycle loads (register-file memory renaming)
zero_cycle_loads.description: A load from a just-stored address is renamed to the register holding the stored value.
zero_cycle_loads.detection_rule: a store and reload through the same base register shortens a load-to-DIV dependency chain; the same address through a different register does not

judgment.text: Present but narrow. Handley's probes speed up only a load that uses the store's address register with an immediate offset, a case ocxtal's tests need not have hit.

banked_prf_power.name: Banked register file with bank power gating
banked_prf_power.description: The register file has four banks that power down separately; waking one costs two or three cycles.
banked_prf_power.detection_rule: a small extra delay at the register-exhaustion knee that appears or vanishes when the delay changes by one cycle

dispatch_buffers.name: Two-level dispatch through unordered buffers
dispatch_buffers.description: Rename writes into unordered dispatch buffers that feed one scheduler queue per unit.
dispatch_buffers.detection_rule: after a long run of ADDs, rename-only instructions (MOV, NOP) run free for about buffer size / drain rate cycles; a filler limited to three integer units fills a 12-entry buffer, not 24

paired_sched_queues.name: Paired scheduler queues
paired_sched_queues.description: Scheduler queues are paired; a queue with nothing ready issues from its partner.
paired_sched_queues.detection_rule: a filler that can issue to only one unit of a pair sees about half the queue capacity of one that can issue to both

immediate_regs.name: Immediate register pool written at rename
immediate_regs.description: A MOV of a non-zero immediate completes at rename into a pool of about 36 registers.
immediate_regs.detection_rule: a MOV #imm filler knee lies about 36-38 above the ADD knee, and up to ~36 padded MOV #imm placed before ADDs do not move the ADD knee

l2_cachelets.name: Per-core L2 cachelets (inner and outer L2)
l2_cachelets.description: The 12 MiB L2 behaves as four 3 MiB cachelets, one beside each core.
l2_cachelets.detection_rule: single-core bandwidth sweeps step at ~3 MiB and ~7.5 MiB, short of the 12 MiB L2

judgment.text: Likely in effect. One core's bandwidth changes at 3 MiB and 7.5 MiB, and S2C's two hashed index bits fit four slices; whether the cachelets are physical is open.

dczva_l2_zero.name: DC ZVA zero-allocates lines in L2
dczva_l2_zero.description: DC ZVA allocates zeroed lines directly in the L2.
dczva_l2_zero.detection_rule: a DC ZVA stream beats the plain-store fill rate beyond L1 and shows no L1 writebacks

nt_load_handling.name: Non-temporal loads skip L1 fill
nt_load_handling.description: Non-temporal loads are not prefetched into the L1.
nt_load_handling.detection_rule: LDNPQ vs LDPQ sweep is equal in L1, LDNPQ lower in L2 with a higher L1 miss count, higher in DRAM

dtlb_piggyback.name: Single-ported dTLB with piggyback ports
dtlb_piggyback.description: One dTLB lookup per cycle, shared with queued requests to the same page.
dtlb_piggyback.detection_rule: three loads per cycle to one page run at full rate; spreading them over three pages 16 KiB apart drops to about 2.5 cycles per three loads, and a new page on every access to about one load per cycle

l1d_banked_piggyback.name: Banked L1D with piggybacked loads and buffered stores
l1d_banked_piggyback.description: Sixteen 16 B banks; loads to one element share an access and stores are buffered.
l1d_banked_piggyback.detection_rule: loads stepping by 256 B fall to one per cycle, by 128 B to about 1.7 and by 64 B to about 2.35, while steps up to 32 B keep three per cycle; stores keep two per cycle out to 128 B steps

l1d_way_lookup.name: L1D way selection without visible misprediction
l1d_way_lookup.description: Loads to random ways run as fast as loads to one way; no way misprediction shows.
l1d_way_lookup.detection_rule: loads that pick one of eight 16 KiB-apart pages at random on every access run no slower than loads to a fixed page once bank collisions are removed

lsu_virtual_prefetch.name: LSU-resident virtual-address prefetcher
lsu_virtual_prefetch.description: The prefetcher trains on every load and store virtual address at the LSU.
lsu_virtual_prefetch.detection_rule: a linear pointer chase keeps its L1 latency across page boundaries out to DRAM, and page-strided chains the prefetcher can follow lose the L1 TLB miss cost; a physical-address prefetcher would restart at each page

l1d_hashed_way.name: L1D way chosen from physical page bits
l1d_hashed_way.description: A line's way seems fixed by a hash of physical page bits.
l1d_hashed_way.detection_rule: pointer chases with node spacing 2^k+64 B reach the full L1 line count for some k and about one way per set for others, with no extra-cycle way-mispredict outliers

content_directed_prefetch.name: Content-directed (data memory-dependent) prefetch
content_directed_prefetch.description: Pointer-like values in filled lines are prefetched into the L2.
content_directed_prefetch.detection_rule: loading a line of pointers makes later chases through those pointers faster although no load ever used their addresses

judgment.text: Both hold. A privileged HID11 bit turns the DMP off on the M1 and M2; no control outside the kernel does, which is what Augury and GoFetch found.

barrier_colors.name: Color-tagged barriers at the L1-L2 boundary
barrier_colors.description: Barriers advance a color tag on memory requests, and ordering is enforced between the L1 and the L2, not in the LSU.
barrier_colors.detection_rule: a DMB between stores that hit in the L1 costs little, while one between stores that miss to the L2 waits for the earlier misses

load_poison_bits.name: Load poison bits for load-load ordering
load_poison_bits.description: A load whose line is modified by another core before it becomes non-speculative is poisoned and replayed or flushed.
load_poison_bits.detection_rule: same-address loads on one core take extra machine clears only when another core writes the line between them

l2_snoop_filter.name: L2 duplicate L1 tags (snoop filter and flush engine)
l2_snoop_filter.description: The L2 keeps duplicate tags of its cores' L1s, filters snoops for them, and drives a flush engine that pulls dirty L1 lines before a core powers down.
l2_snoop_filter.detection_rule: an idle core keeps its L1 contents through the other cores' sharing traffic, and stores to lines no other L1 holds see no snoop delay

l2_way_power.name: L2 way-group sleep and power-down
l2_way_power.description: L2 ways sit in three separately powered groups that sleep after an idle count set by leakage and temperature, or power off when use is concentrated.
l2_way_power.detection_rule: after an idle stretch the first L2 hits take one or two extra cycles, and after long light load the usable L2 capacity drops to two thirds or one third until miss pressure restores it

l2_victim_fill.name: L2 as a selective victim cache for L1 data
l2_victim_fill.description: DRAM fills go to the L1 only; L1 castouts enter the L2 as victims, clean ones only when their set has shown reuse and the L1-L2 path is free.
l2_victim_fill.detection_rule: one pass over a footprint larger than the L1 leaves little for a second pass to hit in the L2, while repeated passes build up L2 hits

judgment.text: Not as stated on the M1. With an inclusive L2, measured by two labs, DRAM fills enter the L2 as well as the L1.

l2_insertion_priority.name: L2 insertion position by line history
l2_insertion_priority.description: L2 victims enter at LRU positions chosen by stream, prefetch and trip bits, so streams and unused prefetches cycle through a few ways.
l2_insertion_priority.detection_rule: a streaming pass over many MiB evicts only an eighth to a quarter of a resident L2 working set

slc_victim_fill.name: SLC filled by L2 victims
slc_victim_fill.description: CPU lines move from L1 to L2 to the SLC as each level evicts them, so a CPU miss does not allocate in the SLC.
slc_victim_fill.detection_rule: the cached region seen by one core extends to about the L2 share plus the SLC, not to the larger of the two

judgment.text: Handley's later readings agree that CPU misses do not allocate in the SLC; his result of about 50 cycles in random boxes fits region prefetch into the L2 better than an SLC prefetcher.

coherence_duplicate_tags.name: Coherence point with duplicate tags
coherence_duplicate_tags.description: Before the SLC, a coherence point holds copies of every cache's L2 tags and states, a tag-only pseudo-L3 that orders same-address requests.
coherence_duplicate_tags.detection_rule: a read of a line held modified in the other cluster returns faster than a DRAM access

slc_sticky_quota.name: SLC sticky lines and group quotas
slc_sticky_quota.description: SLC lines carry a group ID and a sticky bit; driver-set quotas cap each group, and replacement skips sticky lines.
slc_sticky_quota.detection_rule: not visible to CPU-only probes; a GPU or media working set within its quota survives a CPU sweep larger than the SLC

slc_speculative_read.name: DRAM read issued alongside the SLC lookup
slc_speculative_read.description: A latency-sensitive read enters the memory controller pipeline while the coherence and SLC tag checks run, and is killed if either hits.
slc_speculative_read.detection_rule: DRAM-miss latency exceeds SLC-hit latency by no more than the memory controller's own DRAM access time

slc_power_gating.name: SLC way power-down and drowsy SRAM
slc_power_gating.description: The SLC powers down ways to match the share in use and holds idle SRAM at retention voltage, batching low-QoS requests until it wakes.
slc_power_gating.detection_rule: SLC-range latency or capacity right after an idle period differs from that after a warm-up sweep of the same footprint

fabric_qos_credits.name: Credit-gated fabric with QoS bands
fabric_qos_credits.description: Requests carry one of five QoS classes in three bands on six virtual channels; credits gate entry to the fabric and memory controller.
fabric_qos_credits.detection_rule: not visible to a single-core probe; under bulk GPU traffic a latency-bound CPU miss slows less than CPU streaming bandwidth falls

pio_network.name: Separate PIO network
pio_network.description: Device-memory accesses and short control messages such as interprocessor interrupts use a flat network that skips coherence, the SLC and DRAM.
pio_network.detection_rule: device register access and interprocessor interrupt latency stay flat while the memory fabric is saturated

coprocessor_ordering_table.name: Coprocessor memory-ordering table
coprocessor_ordering_table.description: CPU loads and stores to a page with outstanding AMX (or LZ) accesses wait until the L2 reports those accesses done.
coprocessor_ordering_table.detection_rule: a CPU load to a page that an in-flight AMX store targets stalls even at a different address in that page, but not when it goes to another page

power_estimator_throttle.name: Digital power estimator throttling
power_estimator_throttle.description: Per-core event counts feed a power estimate and energy credits that block vector or AMX issue for a cycle or two and steer DVFS.
power_estimator_throttle.detection_rule: dense SIMD loops on every core of a cluster show issue bubbles at an unchanged clock that disappear when one core runs the same loop alone

idle_clock_division.name: Divided clock while the core waits
idle_clock_division.description: A core stalled on DRAM or waiting for an event receives one clock pulse in four instead of a frequency change.
idle_clock_division.detection_rule: core cycles counted per unit of wall time fall by about four during long DRAM-bound stalls or WFE waits, with no DVFS change

simd_power_down.name: SIMD unit power-down with state offload
simd_power_down.description: After a long stretch without SIMD work the SIMD registers move to a low-leakage store and the SIMD unit loses power.
simd_power_down.detection_rule: the first SIMD instruction after a long integer-only stretch costs a fixed extra delay that recurs after each idle stretch

scan_on_fill_nfp.name: Scan-on-fill next-fetch predictor
scan_on_fill_nfp.description: Prefetched instruction lines are scanned for branches before their first use.
scan_on_fill_nfp.detection_rule: after a predictor flush, later taken branches in a recently filled line redirect faster than the first

loop_modes.name: Tiered loop modes
loop_modes.description: Loops run from the instruction queue, a loop buffer or an L0 cache.
loop_modes.detection_rule: a loop body shorter than the 8-wide dispatch group sustaining more than one iteration (taken loop-back branch) per cycle would show loop packing

judgment.text: Handley says the M1 has loop buffers to save energy; a loop's backward branch already costs nothing, so they should not change timing.

fill_forwarding.name: Fill forwarding to waiting loads
fill_forwarding.description: A load that missed the L1 is woken as its line arrives and takes its bytes during the fill, not by replaying afterwards.
fill_forwarding.detection_rule: a pointer chase whose nodes hit in L2 shows a load-to-use latency two or three cycles below the L2 hit latency plus an L1 hit

biased_branch_filter.name: Biased-branch filtering in the front end
biased_branch_filter.description: Branches, indirect branches and CSELs that always go one way are marked at the I-cache, handled as jumps, NOPs or moves, kept out of the main predictors and checked on a lightweight branch unit.
biased_branch_filter.detection_rule: adding many always-taken branches does not raise the misprediction rate of history-dependent branches, while the first flip of such a branch costs a full mispredict

trace_cache.name: Trace cache built on stable taken branches
trace_cache.description: Straight-line runs joined by stable taken branches are copied from the instruction queue into a trace cache, so one fetch can cross several taken branches.
trace_cache.detection_rule: a loop body joined by always-taken branches sustains more than one taken branch per cycle

judgment.text: Not on the M1. ocxtal measured at most one taken branch per cycle, and Handley places the trace cache on the M4.

prefetch_deny_list.name: Prefetch deny list
prefetch_deny_list.description: Addresses of prefetched lines evicted unused enter a small counted table that pushes back or drops later prefetches to them.
prefetch_deny_list.detection_rule: a pattern whose prefetched lines are never used stops adding DRAM traffic after a few repetitions, and resumes once the lines are used on demand

hierarchical_store_queue.name: Hierarchical store queue
hierarchical_store_queue.description: A primary store queue holds the oldest stores, serves three load searches at once and writes to the L1; younger stores wait in a slower secondary queue searched one load at a time.
hierarchical_store_queue.detection_rule: with many older stores in flight, forwarding from one of the youngest stores takes about 11 cycles instead of about 4

judgment.text: Not in this form on the M1. The two-queue design comes from a post-M1 patent; the M1's 60 stores fit one queue, banked as Handley guesses from the mixed-stream stall.

early_barrier_completion.name: Early barrier completion
early_barrier_completion.description: ISB and DSB flush younger work at decode and complete once the relevant older instructions finish, poisoning rare conflicting instructions instead of waiting for the barrier to reach the ROB head.
early_barrier_completion.detection_rule: an ISB or DSB costs little more than a refetch when no older memory or system-register work is pending, and its cost grows with outstanding older loads and stores rather than with older ALU work

judgment.text: Not on the M1 for DSB. A DSB alone does not stop speculation past a mispredicted branch on the M1; the design comes from post-M1 patents.

coherence_directory.name: Coherence directory at the SLC
coherence_directory.description: A hashed, set-associative directory at the SLC records which L2-level caches hold each line, replacing duplicate tags; a set overflow invalidates a line in its L2.
coherence_directory.detection_rule: lines cached in several L2s are invalidated well below the L2s' combined capacity when their addresses crowd one directory set

ipv_replacement.name: Criticality-aware replacement vectors
ipv_replacement.description: Cache replacement order is updated by small insertion/promotion vectors chosen by each line's prefetched and critical bits.
ipv_replacement.detection_rule: in a contended set, prefetched lines never used are evicted before demand lines of the same age, and page-table or instruction lines outlast both

fetch_page_split.name: Fetch split at page boundaries
fetch_page_split.description: A fetch that crosses a page boundary takes two cycles, one per page; within a page fetch delivers up to 16 instructions, one 64 B line, per cycle.
fetch_page_split.detection_rule: A loop whose first instruction sits in the last 4 bytes of a page costs one cycle more per iteration than the same loop placed within one page.

l1d_utag_way_predictor.name: Virtual-address utag way predictor
l1d_utag_way_predictor.description: The L1D picks its way through an 8-bit micro-tag folded by XOR from virtual address bits 47:14, as in AMD's linear-address utag scheme, on both core types.
l1d_utag_way_predictor.detection_rule: In AMD's utag test, address pairs whose 8-bit XOR folds of bits 47:14 match show the alias slowdown and other pairs do not.

store_address_data_uops.name: Store address and store data uops
store_address_data_uops.description: A store issues as a store-address uop and a store-data uop; Apple's guide gives the P-core up to two of each per cycle beside three load uops.
store_address_data_uops.detection_rule: A store whose data waits on a long-latency op still issues its address, so a younger load to another address is not held behind it.

lsu_forward_progress.name: Load-store forward-progress widgets
lsu_forward_progress.description: Counters watch for victimized lock lines and repeated replays of the oldest load or store and step in by stalling issue, and LFSR-driven random stalls at issue, replay, retire and drain points break up livelocks.
lsu_forward_progress.detection_rule: A probe that keeps the oldest load replaying, or makes two cores fight over one locked line, would see bursts of extra stall cycles and timing noise rather than a hang.

forced_nonspec_mode.name: Forced non-speculative execution
forced_nonspec_mode.description: Control bits stop the core from speculating past HVC or guarded-mode calls, while single-stepping, or when the speculative flush pointer is invalid while an MP condition holds, for a time set by a timer select.
forced_nonspec_mode.detection_rule: A load placed after an HVC that never returns to it would leave a cache footprint only while HVC speculation is on.

itlb_victims_to_dtlb.name: L1 dTLB as backing store for the iTLBs
itlb_victims_to_dtlb.description: Translations evicted from the user or kernel L1 iTLB move into the shared L1 dTLB; loads cannot see the iTLB itself.
itlb_victims_to_dtlb.detection_rule: after code on a page is fetched, a load to that page misses the L1 dTLB until 4 or more branches 32 x 16 KB apart push the translation out of the iTLB, after which the load hits

exclusive_monitor_l1.name: Exclusive monitor bound to L1D residency
exclusive_monitor_l1.description: A load-exclusive reservation lasts only while its line stays in the L1D, so evicting the line makes the store-exclusive fail; each core holds one reservation with a 64 B granule.
exclusive_monitor_l1.detection_rule: LDXR a line, walk an 8-address L1D eviction set for it, then STXR; the store fails exactly when the line left the L1D

l2_autolock.name: Inclusive L2 that spares L1-resident lines (AutoLock)
l2_autolock.description: The L2 is inclusive of the L1Ds, and its replacement takes lines with no L1D copy before lines an L1D still holds.
l2_autolock.detection_rule: an L2 eviction set walked on another core evicts a line from this core's L1D only when the set's own lines all stay in L1D, split over the two L1D sets of one 128 B L2 line

slc_hashed_index.name: Hashed SLC set index
slc_hashed_index.description: The SLC picks one of 4,096 sets with 12 index bits, each an XOR of several physical address bits from bit 7 up, so addresses spread nearly evenly over the sets.
slc_hashed_index.detection_rule: SLC eviction sets fall into 4,096 congruence classes, and a buffer strided by up to 8 KiB still reaches about 90% of the SLC.

load_address_prediction.name: Load address prediction
load_address_prediction.description: A PC-tagged predictor loads from a strided address before the real address is known; absent on M1, present from M2/A15.
load_address_prediction.detection_rule: a chain of dependent loads whose addresses stride by 32 B keeps the per-load latency of a random-order chain; with the predictor it speeds up after about 120 to 500 loads

tso_mode.name: Runtime-selectable TSO memory model
tso_mode.description: A privileged control bit switches a core to x86-TSO ordering for Rosetta while keeping out-of-order loads.
tso_mode.detection_rule: with ACTLR_EL1.EnTSO set, cache-hitting loads wider than 16 B run over 10x slower on an M1 P core and an 8-byte load forwarded from a 4-byte store runs several times slower than with the bit clear

store_merge_buffer.name: Store merge buffer
store_merge_buffer.description: Stores wait in a store merge buffer (SMB) that drains by a programmable threshold, and a store held there can be invalidated.
store_merge_buffer.detection_rule: A burst of stores to one small chunk of a line writes the L1D fewer times than it has stores, so it outruns the L1D store rate until the drain threshold forces the buffer out.

snoop_starvation_guard.name: Snoop starvation safeguards
snoop_starvation_guard.description: The L2 has a starvation mode that snoop evictions of exclusive-monitor lines can trigger, and the core reserves eviction-buffer credits for snoops so they are not starved.
snoop_starvation_guard.detection_rule: LDXR/STXR loops on one line while another core floods it with snoops would show stretches of no progress ended by a sudden recovery when the starvation mode starts.

cluster_sleep_states.name: Core and cluster sleep states
cluster_sleep_states.description: WFI either only clock-gates a core or lets it power down, chosen in CPU_OVRD; cluster deep sleep sets ACC_OVRD fields for the L2 flush, SRM and CPM power-down and link train-down, and branch predictor state can be kept across cluster sleep.
cluster_sleep_states.detection_rule: Wake-up delay after idle falls into distinct levels (clock-gated, core powered down, cluster in deep sleep), and branch mispredicts right after a cluster wake show whether predictor state survived.

fast_ipi.name: Fast IPIs through system registers
fast_ipi.description: A core interrupts another by writing a system register with an immediate, deferred, retract or no-wake request; a deferred request waits for a countdown in reference-clock ticks set in a global register.
fast_ipi.detection_rule: A cross-core ping-pong through the IPI request register has a much shorter round trip than one through the interrupt controller, and a deferred request arrives only after the programmed countdown.

exec_clock_gating.name: Clock gating of idle execution pipes
exec_clock_gating.description: Integer execution (IEX) clocks and the prefetcher training pipe are clock-gated when idle, with tunables that force the clocks on or limit the gating.
exec_clock_gating.detection_rule: The first integer ops after a long stretch of non-integer work issue a cycle or more late, a delay that a steady integer loop never shows.
